quotes.notes: It was easy to know what happened. They jumped and went for three furlongs and Ryan [Moore] made that decision when they were going that he was going to take his time on Minnie Hauk. That was the right thing to do but then the pace went out of the race so Ryan ended up in a slowly run mile and a quarter on a mile and a half filly and he had no chance then. With her, you'd want an end-to-end mile and a quarter at the top level for her to come into her best. She'll leave that run well behind her I'd imagine and, if we did go to Royal Ascot [for the Prince of Wales's] she'd be going forward and there'd be no taking back - Aidan O'Brien, trainer, speaking on Racing TV.

quotes.raceTitle: Clem Murphy Memorial Irish EBF Mooresbridge Stakes (Group 2)
quotes.notes: You'd be delighted with that. We wanted a nice, even pace so Minnie Hauk could get back into gear a little bit. We didn't want a dawdle, so it was lovely for her. She travelled with all the zest she did last year and won very snugly. You couldn't be happier with her and Ryan was very happy. He said he just let her point her toe a bit the last furlong. The Tattersalls Gold Cup is the plan, and that was the perfect prep for it. If the Tattersalls Gold Cup went well, she could go to Ascot for the Prince of Wales's. We were thinking of keeping her at a mile and a quarter for her first three runs - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

They just went very fast and Minnie Hauk just got trapped out a little bit. I think she'll stay [in training] next year - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.Minnie Hauk never really settled, and when I asked her to take some blows, she never took it. So I think she just over-raced today - Christophe Soumillon, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: Qatar Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe (Group 1) (3yo+ No Geldings) (Grande Course) (Turf)
quotes.notes: Minnie Hauk ran a great race. We're delighted with her. We'll get her home and see how she is and make a decision [on her participation at the Breeders' Cup] - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.We're very proud of Minnie Hauk she just got caught. She's run a blinder. I thought she'd won and I'm sure she's got a great future, and I look forward to her running many more times - Michael Tabor, co-owner.Minnie Hauk is a big galloper and she took the front so easily. When she came on the bit I thought, 'Now it's time to go', and we are going to win easy, but I was squeezing her to keep going. If you take Daryz out, she would be one of the most impressive fillies to win the Arc, but that is racing. Sometimes you just have to accept you get beaten by another one - Christophe Soumillon, jockey.

Minnie Hauk cruises and she's a lovely mover, and obviously the Arc and the Breeders' Cup Turf are there for her. A lot of people have done a lot to look after her, so I appreciate everyone's hard work and I'm delighted. Ryan gave her a class ride and he was very cool on her. She's classy and it was a very confident ride. It wasn't going to be a micky mouse race, they were going to go an even gallop without going crazy. It's up to the lads. Ryan said possibly the Arc for Whirl and the Breeders' Cup for this filly depending on ground. Whirl, as we saw at Goodwood, handles soft ground, but she handles the other ground as well. Minnie Hauk has run on soft ground, but we always thought the quicker the ground the better she'd be, and she skipped over that. She has a lot of options, but the better the race the better she'll be - Aidan O'Brien, trainer, speaking to ITV Racing.

The boss [John Magnier] said he asked Ryan where to go with Minnie Hauk and he said she could go to the Yorkshire Oaks and the boss said what about giving her a break and train her for the Vermeille to give her a French prep for the Arc. So all those things are open.  I think she can do either those things but if she was going down the Arc trial route, she'd have to have a couple of easy weeks and obviously if she was going to York then she wouldn't have those couple easy weeks. She had a very easy race today as the tempo wasn't strong so she should come out of it well. I'd imagine we'd have a fair idea in the next week. Looking at her, she probably would love York - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

I'm delighted with Minnie Hauk. She's very classy and Ryan gave her a beautiful ride. He loved her the last day [at Chester] and then again today, so she's very exciting. She's obviously learning - she went to Chester and learnt a lot and was still green, and she was always improving from mid-race. What you love about her is that she's a great traveller; she has a lot of class. Ryan felt he was going very easily today on her and usually what that means is that she will be able to step up a couple of grades into even higher-class races. It's lovely for the lads and for everyone to have another filly like that. - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.Minnie Hauk is still learning a little bit. Aidan had a lot of faith in her. She travelled around strongly and I got to her quite easy, and then she was a little green in front. When the other filly came back she went on again. She's a talented filly and she stayed on well. I'm very happy with her and hopefully she'll build on this - Ryan Moore, jockey.

That [the Oaks] is the plan. Aidan always thought Minnie Hauk would improve a lot for this run. She's a very kind, uncomplicated filly with a great attitude. The step up in trip obviously helped and you'd be thinking of the Oaks. Ryan was niggling away just to get her interested, but she's kind and always answers to the jockey and she just kept on finding. Ryan was quite sweet on her - Paul Smith, representative of Coolmore, owners.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: She had a fantastic season last year, winning the Oaks, Irish Oaks and Yorkshire Oaks before her second in the Arc, which was a great run. Maybe with the benefit of hindsight we should have finished up with her after that and left her alone, because she was only a three-year-old filly. There's no doubt she's stronger this year - she's twice as wide and we couldn't have been happier with her at the Curragh on Sunday morning, she came up in front. She seems in great form. She'll probably be trained for the Tattersalls Gold Cup and could go to the Mooresbridge on the way. Then she might go to Ascot for the Prince of Wales's Stakes as we think she might be the one of ours best suited to it. She could then go back up to a mile and a half and could definitely end up in the Arc again, but it's going to depend on how the three-year-olds fare as well. 31-03-26

I just kept filling him up and I could feel at halfway he was coming good. He came alive at the two pole and it was just a case of getting the run out of him. He has won from the back over five furlongs before, so I knew he had the turn of foot - Jamie Spencer, rider

quotes.raceTitle: Net World Sports Queensferry Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.notes: We put a line through his last performance at Newbury when Mitbaahy was drawn on the wrong side of the track. He'd also been on the wrong side at Haydock, while he also ran better than his finishing position at Ascot. So while his form figures weren't that flattering, his runs had been better than they looked. I think winning has opened up some more options for him going into the autumn. He's in the Sprint Cup at Haydock and I think he'll get an entry for the Champions Sprint at Ascot too - Roger Varian, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Dubai International Airport World Trophy Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.notes: Mitbaahy is in the Abbaye, but I'm not sure if he'll go there. There is Champions Day and he's a nice horse - Roger Varian, trainer.

Mitbaahy was very good last time at Hamilton and we are starting to work him out now he is getting stronger. He is a talented horse. He won't run at Royal Ascot. He was put in that in case he didn't win here today and then we would have looked to exploit his handicap mark. The most obvious place to go is to come back here on Coral Eclipse Day for the Charge, which is over five furlongs - Roger Varian, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He came to us at the end of last year and I love how laid-back he is for a sprinter. He's straightforward to deal with and pretty bombproof really. I couldn't have been any happier with his first run for us when fourth in the Abernant, but over five furlongs at Newmarket in the Palace House they were always going a stride too quick for him. He then beat two Group 1 winners in the Greenlands Stakes last month and the stiff track at the Curragh really seemed to suit him. He clearly gets six furlongs well and the target at this stage is the Queen Elizabeth II Jubilee Stakes but if the ground were to come up very soft on Tuesday, then I think we'd look at the King Charles III Stakes over five furlongs. Either way, the track will suit him and Jamie Spencer rides.

He enjoyed a good campaign in 2022 and it was great to see him back in the winner's enclosure last time when taking the Listed Queensferry Stakes at Chester in good style. He had his excuses earlier in the year and now he's back to form we could look at the Haydock Sprint Cup. He's pretty useful on his day. 25-08-23

quotes.notes: I thought Unequal Love might run well but I wasn't expecting Montassib to enjoy that ground and I thought they were both drawn away from the real action. We relied on Bucanero Fuerte going forward, which he did, and Unequal Love was always travelling well, whereas Cieren [Fallon] had to get after Montassib. On softer ground they come back to him and that would suit him better, but he's the most genuine horse at home and Cieren always thinks there's more to come. The Champions Sprint was always the race I was looking forward to. You would think the race would suit him, but he'll now be one of the favourites and things are different when you're expected to win - William Haggas, trainer.

quotes.notes: I'm not sure where we'll go now, but Montassib won't go to Goodwood for the Stewards' Cup. He'd have to carry a Group-race penalty now. I think we'll stick to stakes races and go wherever we can get a bit of dig in the ground - William Haggas, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: William Hill Cammidge Trophy Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.notes: I do believe I should have won the Ayr Gold Cup on Montassib, he reversed the form at York and he's improving all the time. He's got so much quicker - Cieren Fallon, rider.

"It's only taken us three years to find Montassib's right trip, but we got there in the end. He had a bit more luck than he did at Ayr. He really is a lovely horse and one of those nice ones to have around. He was a good two-year-old then had a problem with his heart, and had the whole three-year-old campaign off. He's still got a few miles on the clock and lots of racing left in him. There isn't much left for him unless something comes up at Doncaster, but that might be it for the year. He's definitely stepped up his last two runs" - Maureen Haggas, assistant trainer.

Montassib found the ground quick enough but I wanted to make the most of him by setting him alight two and a half furlongs out. It's nice that he could get his head back in front - Cieren Fallon, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: William Hill Pick Your Places Handicap
quotes.notes: I thought Montassib was certain not to cope with conditions and told everyone he'd dislike the ground, but he coped with them. Most Exceed And Excels don't like that ground, but he won nicely and I don't know what we'll do, but the Buckingham Palace Stakes at Royal Ascot would seem an obvious target - William Haggas, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Watch Racing TV In Stunning HD Novice Stakes
quotes.notes: It was probably as you'd have hoped from Montassib. Four-runner races can get a bit muddly but he travelled into the race and duly put his head in front. He's had a good experience, the ground is plenty quick enough and he handled that fine. It's good to have him back on the racecourse. He looks like he belongs in a Newbury or Ascot paddock and hopefully he'll be ending up at those racetracks in the near future - Tom Marquand, jockey.

A lot of credit goes to to John Hammond [racing manager to Gerard Augustin-Normand] because it wasn't my idea to run. Monteille worked well and he urged me to run. When she picked up she was really good. She really needed her comeback and she was very impressive today. We'll see how she comes out of the race but I think the owners would like to go to Ascot - Mario Baratti, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: She's been in good form since her win at Chantilly, though we haven't had to do a lot with her. She'll have one light canter in the middle of this week and then the partners will decide together, but Ascot remains an option. She's in the Goffs London Sale before the meeting. 11-06-25

I need to watch to watch the race again but for me they didn't go fast at all and he really struggled to get momentum. I think More Thunder is better going fast Tom came in and said if we run over this trip again they'll need to go hard. He feels 6f is his best distance. I think he deserves a shot at a Group race now. We had wanted to go up to seven at some stage and today was a good opportunity. We'll have a crack at a six-furlong sprint now ? he's in everything. He only won when his head was down but this year there have been a lot of times when my head has been up and we've got beat -  William Haggas, trainer.
Delighted with the way More Thunder ran, a little frustrated with the outcome - William Haggas, trainer.

At some stage More Thunder is going to go into stakes races, but he's low enough in the handicap to be competitive [in the Wokingham]. He had three pounds less weight than he should have had today, and that would've made the difference so the handicapper shouldn't put him up too much - William Haggas, trainer.

More Thunder travelled very well and finished his race off well. Wiliam Haggas wanted to start him off over six with a view to going seven furlongs next time. He's strengthened up and has been showing more speed this year - Philip Robinson, racing manager to owner Saeed Suhail.

quotes.raceTitle: British Stallion Studs EBF Stonehenge Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.notes: It was a good race, the second is a smart horse who ran well at Ascot last time out. Morris Dancer was finishing well at Goodwood and the step up to a mile suited him. He's still learning, it's only his fourth start, he was a bit green in front so hopefully he can take another step forward. He's not the tallest but he's got plenty of strength. He just bounced out of Goodwood and was doing all his best work late and, with the ground in good condition, we thought we'd come here. It's fantastic for his sire Palace Pier, who's going great guns. We've put him in the Champagne and could drop him back in trip. We'll see how he comes out of this and make a plan - Thady Gosden, joint-trainer.

We're thrilled with Morris Dancer, he's run a great race. He won at Haydock and he just had a little bit of a niggle, so we backed off. He's come here on the minimum work and he's run a great race. William [Buick] said don't be frightened stepping up to a mile, so we'll go a mile somewhere next - John Gosden, joint-trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Anglesey Lodge Equine Hospital Woodlands Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.notes: We thought Moss Tucker might need the run like he's done the last couple of seasons but as Billy (Lee, jockey) said it was a very good performance off ten stone. He seemed very relaxed in the prelims, was good in the gates and just went up through the gears. Billy said he had a little blow, as you'd expect, at the half-furlong pole but he has a touch of class about him and knows his job. Hopefully he might be able to go to the Greenlands if the ground was suitable, he doesn't have to have it heavy or very soft but once there's kindness in it we'll be looking at the likes of that. It fits in well and then he has two entries at Royal Ascot but obviously the ground is a proviso there too - Ken Condon, trainer, speaking on Racing TV

quotes.raceTitle: Al Basti Equiworld, Dubai Flying Five Stakes (Group 1)
quotes.notes: Moss Tucker has been a great story with how he has progressed. Going in here we would have been delighted to be placed and then the heavens opened which helped us a good bit. He was very good here last time a month ago in the Phoenix Stakes, which was a career best and this was another one - Ken Condon, trainer.

The Abbaye has been the plan all year. Moss Tucker ran well there last season after missing the break and does handle those testing conditions. He might go straight there but if the ground is on the right side for him in the Flying Five he'll go here. He was good out there today. He enjoyed it and Billy said he never thought they were going to get to him. He just lengthened all the way to the line. He didn't have the likes of Art Power to contend with but he was good and for a sprinter he's ultra-reliable. He goes better when its heavy or testing but seems to go on all ground - Ken Condon, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Hatstone Solicitors Waterford Testimonial Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.notes: Moss Tucker is very honest, reliable and solid and he is still improving. He is very straightforward and I hope he will have a productive year again next year - Ken Condon, trainer.

We've asked Moss Tucker to run two quick races before. He's a very relaxed horse and is very tough, very likeable. He's got better with racing and has a good record at this track. We ran Ombudsman a little tenderly last year, listed, Ryan [Moore] rode him in Deauville, won a Group 3, put him away. quotes.notes: Precise was very special last year and only just made the Guineas [at Newmarket]. Because she's a homebred it makes it very special. It's difficult to breed a Classic winner - next to impossible - so when it happens it's very exciting. We knew there was massive improvement and, in all fairness to Ryan Moore [rider of True Love], it was a difficult decision [on who to ride]. Wayne was super cool on the winner but Ryan had to ride True Love this time. We knew it was possible this could happen. It was an even pace, but Wayne said when he started to move and put her into top gear, she just took off and said she ran through the line. We came here thinking it was possible she could go back to Epsom in two weeks if the lads decide to do that. It would be very exciting and another very difficult decision for Ryan, as Amelia Earhart is in there and favourite. Will Precise get a mile and a half- You don't know until you try it but she's out of a Galileo mare [Way To My Heart] with a lot of stamina in her pedigree, so there's every chance she would even though she's by Starspangledbanner. It's exciting and I'm delighted for everybody - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

Precise looks serious and a special filly. Everything she has done from day one has been so easy. We weren't sure how good she was but she looks a serious filly, make no mistake. That was even more impressive than Minding. Don't get me wrong, Minding was a top filly but this filly is different gear. We put those two fillies in there to make it a good strong gallop and she came through it great and gets better with every run. Christophe was sitting motionless most of the way and she does it so easy. I think she's a Classic filly. They'll both [Precise and Diamond Necklace] be trained for the Guineas, whether it be France, Britain or Ireland. The lads will decide. I don't think we'll see either of them again this year. When you get a special one you have to look after them - Aidan O'Brien. trainer.I was impressed when Precise won last time at the Curragh and came past us in three strides [when Soumillon was aboard favourite Composing in the Group One Moyglare]. She looks she can still improve a lot and loves to have horses to target. She missed the jump a bit, so I came behind Wayne [Lordan, on Composing] and she was really cruising the whole way. When I asked her to quicken, I came a bit early I think but when I asked her to go, she went past them like a train - Christophe Soumillon, jockey.

Precise is a lovely filly. She's growing and maturing all of the time. You don't know when she'll stop improving and she's very classy. She travelled very strongly and galloped right through the line. That was a win and you're in for the Breeders' Cup and she'd love that fast ground, she's a slick mover. Now she's a Group 1 winner we can go gentle with her - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

Precise is a very professional filly. She has pace, and what you like about her is that when you get down into her she gets seven [furlongs] quite well. She looked comfortable. We gave her a day away at the Curragh and we'll take her back and train her for Newmarket and see what happens. I was super-impressed with her when she won the Fillies' Mile last year - she went through the last furlong coasting. She then travelled over for the Breeders' Cup and all we thought she had to do was get round, but she picked up an infection. She's not overly big but is still 30kg up on last year's racing weight, which doesn't usually happen with a filly of that size. I'd imagine she'll end up going straight to the 1,000 Guineas and then go to the Oaks after that. Plenty are saying she's by Starspangledbanner so won't stay a mile and a half, but my instinct is that she's an incredible filly. I could be totally wrong, we've only trained a few Starspangledbanners, but everything she does suggests she'll stay. She has loads of personality, but she relaxes. 31-03-26

quotes.raceTitle: Bet Boost At bet365 Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
quotes.notes: I think Prince Of India is ready to step up in class and once he gets some more give in the ground he'll appreciate that too. I think he's fast enough for this distance and as he gets stronger he will develop into a real sprinter. I do think there's more to come - Marco Botti, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Coolmore Stud No Nay Never Fairy Bridge Stakes (Group 3) (Fillies & Mares)
quotes.notes: If any horse deserved to win a stakes race, it is Princess Child, but you don't always get what you deserve. I don't know how many times she has been placed in stakes races without winning one, and we were campaigning her aggressively to win one. She had built a whole load of black type, but you have to win one too. I would say that will be a career best, and when a horse wins a race they get confidence from it. We'll see where next, but she is a Group winner now, which is kind of job done, but we will try and win another one now - Joseph O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Ahonoora Handicap (Premier Handicap)
quotes.notes: Once we straightened up I knew I would pick them up because they were kind of paddling in front. Princess Child is a very consistent filly and hopefully she can progress into stakes company again and get her head in front - Dylan Browne McMonagle, jockey.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: She's got better every year with racing and ran great when second in the Express Stakes behind Celestial Orbit last time after not doing badly in a messy race on her comeback. She could take on Celestial Orbit again in the Lanwades Stud Stakes. 22-04-26

quotes.notes: He has an unbelievable pedigree and was just raw and babyish the first day. Even today Proposition was still very raw but when Ronan (Whelan) galvanised him, he galloped out strong to the line. He'll be a lovely middle-distance horse for next year, he handles that ground and will get further. He isn't too bad - Chris Armstrong, stable representative

quotes.raceTitle: British Stallion Studs John Dunlop EBF Conditions Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.notes: It's not a huge surprise that Protection Act was able to take a step up in grade but he's a horse who we've minded through the spring and just allowed him to come to hand when he's ready. He's obviously achieved plenty over a mile so far, but it would be no surprise to see him get further. He relaxes and seems to find the line. There are lots of options for a horse like him. He could go to something like the Heron Stakes [on May 28], and he's in the St James's Palace at Royal Ascot. All options really are open for him at the moment - George Boughey, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He's a big, rangy horse who did everything on raw ability last year. He's taken a bit of time to come to hand this spring but will improve as the summer goes on and we might miss the Craven meeting. I think he'll be seen to better effect when he goes up in trip, possibly to ten furlongs. He'd be near the top of the pile and is really exciting. 02-04-26

quotes.notes: Puerto Rico looked a little bit rusty on his first run of the year so we'll try again. I think a mile will be his trip - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

Puerto Rico is pacey, he stays and we wanted to see what he would be like over a mile. He handles soft ground, although we were thinking of going to the Breeders' Cup with him, but when Gstaad went to the Breeders' Cup, we said we'd let him come here. He'll start in a Guineas. He's a classy horse who I see as a real miler but because he's so relaxed I think he will get further - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.Puerto Rico has a lot of talent, but he's a horse who looks around a bit and you have to make sure he concentrates. He was a little bit upset in the stalls but I made sure we got a good start because he's very happy when he can dominate from the front. I wanted to go forward and I saw that the horse we had to beat [Cape Orator] was upsides but wasn't travelling as well on the home turn. I got a good blow into him there and I knew he'd see the trip out well. He looks like he'll be a very good horse at this trip next year - Christophe Soumillon, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: Qatar Prix Jean-Luc Lagardere (Group 1) (2yo Colts & Fillies) (New Course) (Turf)
quotes.notes: I was probably running Puerto Rico over a little bit too short because he was showing us loads of speed. He ran over six furlongs up until Doncaster. That was his first run over seven and he won. The horse that was third to him that day [Cape Orator] won yesterday, so the form got very strong overnight. Christophe [Soumillon] gave him a beautiful ride. He's a lovely, big, powerful, mature horse with loads of speed. The lads were thinking of the Breeders' Cup and they asked about ground, but Christophe said ground and trip would be no problem. I'd say he definitely could be one for the Juvenile Turf - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.Ryan [Moore, jockey] said he thought the ground would be a big help to Puerto Rico and for me to ride him confidently, and it was the same with Aidan before the race. There's nothing hard, we ride for the horses. He jumped the gates really well and I took him to the front and he was really relaxed. He was hanging out for a while but in the straight when I took him to the rail he picked up really well and I felt nobody was following me - Christophe Soumillon, jockey.

That was very polished. Puerto Rico is a nice horse and showed a great attitude, Sean was very happy with him. He's not ground dependent and he's been knocking on the door, I thought he ran particularly well in the Richmond Stakes at Goodwood. It's nice to get his Group 2 win on the board and it's been a while since Seahenge won this for us, and Westphalia before that. He's by the sire of the moment Wootton Bassett out of a Galileo mare and he's got a very good pedigree. I haven't had a chance to speak to Aidan but he's entered up in all the right places so he's a horse to look forward to - Kevin Buckley, Coolmore representative.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He's a very good horse and could be anything. He missed two months early last year, so he was a good bit behind everyone else and was probably playing catch-up all the time. I was running him over six furlongs early in the year and I remember he was flat out the whole way in the Richmond and still finished second. He just kept progressing - he improved when he went from six to seven furlongs, winning the Champagne Stakes and the Lagardere, then again up to a mile when he won another Group 1 in France. He's done very well physically. He's scopey, strong and his mind has really gone the right way. He could be one to take on the older milers and travel to all the big Group 1s. He's very uncomplicated; he can make the running or drop in. 31-03-26

quotes.notes: When I rode Purosangue the last day, he bumped into a really nice horse of Karl's (Burke, trainer). I was very confident he'd stay the six and he stayed well. He was a willing partner who has been so consistent all year and deserved to finish off the year on a high note. He wouldn't be the biggest but he's solid. He's got great mental strength and I'd be confident he'd train on" - P J McDonald, jockey.

We're just thrilled Purosangue is back on form - he created a very good impression first time out, and we just thought he did things the wrong way round at Newmarket. That was much more like it, and he was beaten by a very good horse. He won on pretty good ground at Haydock so I think he's quite versatile. He looks like he'll be made for the Roses at York - Andrew Balding, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He's a nice horse who we inherited from Andrew Balding. He was a useful horse for him last year in top-notch handicaps (fourth in the Ayr Gold Cup). He has run only once for us, at Pontefract in early April. He missed the break, started late and actually made up a lot of ground, finishing fourth in quite a decent 6f handicap won by Arklow Lad. He ran a belter at Newbury on Saturday, finishing fourth, but he would have been at least placed had he not got hemmed in. If there's any soft in the going description it will enhance his prospects and I think he's got a nice big handicap in him this year. 20-05-26

quotes.raceTitle: Childwickbury Stud Fillies' Trial Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.notes: I was really disappointed at Newmarket. We wanted to roll forward but Falakeyah was just too quick for us and Qilin Queen didn't come down the Dip too well either. I told Hollie Doyle to be bold today because she keeps galloping and she nailed it. She wasn't very good in the prelims before her last run but she was much better today. She was still a bit buzzy but that's just her and not something I'd worry about. If all is well we'll probably roll the dice at Epsom. She's very game, athletic and will stay well - Ed Walker, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Tattersalls £40,000 EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.notes: Qilin Queen is a nice filly going forward. She made a pleasing debut at Newbury but was quite green that day. It was noticeable how professional she was today and she's a tall, leggy filly who'll strengthen and improve for the year. I've no doubt she'll  train on and make a nice 3yo too - Ross Coakley, jockey, talking to RacingTV.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: It's lovely to have her back. She had a great time in 2025 and we'll try to get her some Group 1 form this year. She could start in the Nottinghamshire Oaks over 1m2f or join American Gal in the Dahlia Stakes at Newmarket. If she doesn't look like being competitive at the top level here, we could look at races on grass in America. She goes on fast ground, is well balanced, not very big and good out of the stalls. 22-04-26

quotes.notes: Qirat has always threatened to be a good horse, I've just never managed to get it out of him until today. He was here to set the pace and go 12-second furlongs from the front. That's what he was here to do and the longer he lasted, the better it was for everyone concerned with him. That was the idea. Having watched the clock, I think he achieved that, and the last thing I said to Richard Kingscote before he got on him was, 'Keep going on this fellow. He isn't going to stop and he could run really well here' - Ralph Beckett, trainer. I feel like a villain, but when I saw it wasn't a grey nose coming towards me I kept going. Ultimately, we were there as a helping hand to go an even gallop and we were somewhat ignored early then took a lead off Wayne Lordan. Towards the cutaway I was thinking Qirat was going well, but you always expect the horses rated 20lb higher to be coming through. I could see Rosallion coming, but my horse kept pulling out. I think Ralph [Beckett, trainer] was happy to have me on as I like being in front, like my fractions and it worked out okay. It's a bit surreal but great to be going to Hong Kong on a positive note - Richard Kingscote, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: William Hill Most Top Price Runners Handicap
quotes.notes: Conditions hadn't gone Qirat's way but he was at his best back on the easier surface. I've always thought he was well handicapped and with a bit of rain he may well have won the Britannia at Royal Ascot - Hector Crouch, rider, speaking to ITV Racing.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: I can't say any of us were expecting him to win the Sussex, but Richard Kingscote was brilliant on him. He was in the best shape he'd been in all year and that combination meant it all came to pass. We're likely to go back to Goodwood for the Celebration Mile and the Sussex again. He might go for the Diomed on Derby weekend along the way. 27-04-26

quotes.raceTitle: Singspiel Stakes Sponsored By Emirates Airline (Group 2) (Turf)
quotes.notes: There was no pace early. Ryan [Moore] had Quddwah in completely the right position, he kicked off the bend and won very well. We'll see how he is but I think that's the plan [The Dubai Turf on World Cup Night], it's a win and you're in and he saw out the extra furlong well - Ed Crisford, joint-trainer, speaking to Racing TV.Quddwah is a very straightforward horse who is very consistent at this level. The race worked out nicely for him and he showed a good attitude. It was a solid performance - Ryan Moore, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: Zabeel Mile Sponsored By Phi Advertising (Group 2) (Turf)
quotes.notes: We didn't go that quick and I was happy to press on early with Quddwah. He stuck at it well. He's been very consistent over the years and he always gives his running. - James Doyle, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

We're delighted with Quddwah. Ascot was very excusable as it was too quick that day and he didn't let himself down on the ground. When he's got these sorts of conditions he's a very good horse, as you saw today. We'll talk to Sheikh Ahmed and see what he would like to do for the future, but races like the Celebration Mile, the Jacques le Marois and the Prix du Moulin all come into discussions. We'll see how he is after the race and make a plan - Simon Crisford, joint-trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Prix du Haras de Fresnay-le-Buffard Jacques le Marois (Group 1) (3yo+ No Geldings) (Straight Course)
quotes.notes: I thought Quddwah ran super, obviously lacking experience going into a championship race. The ground was a little bit quick for him and I think his career is all ahead of him. I think it was a very solid run and we'll look forward to seeing him on his next start. We'll talk to [owner] Sheikh Ahmed and see what he wants to do, but an obvious next race would be the Leopardstown Mile - Simon Crisford, joint-trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Bet With Ascot Donation Scheme Paradise Stakes (A Queen Anne Stakes Trial) (Listed Race)
quotes.notes: Quddwah won at Newmarket nicely and we were due to run him at the July meeting in a Listed race, but just before he got a little issue and we had to put him away. However, he'd always shown he was a horse on the up. We'll have to see what Sheikh Ahmed [Al Maktoum, owner] wants to do but the Diomed is probably the next step up. He's a bit immature and Epsom might be a lot, but we have to look at what the options are and he just wants bringing along in a nice manner. He is in the Queen Anne and I don't think I'd have reservations about that, because he'll come on a lot from this and it just depends on what happens in the next few weeks. This is only his third race, so he's still got his whole future ahead of him. He's a very nice horse to have in the stable. He picked up well and finished off nicely, showing a lovely turn of foot. I think today's small field with this ground was the perfect start of him - Ed Crisford, joint-trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: William Hill Lengthen Your Odds Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.notes: Quddwah had to be quite brave as the second took us off a line a bit but he showed a real likeable attitude. I'd never sat on him, but he's got a good pedigree and will go further - he's got a lovely relaxed character and should improve for further. The ground is on the dead side of good, it's not bad, and rode quite nice on him. The third horse gives some substance to the form and I'd say the race will work out. He's got a bit of quality - James Doyle, jockey.

Queen All Star is a lovely filly. We thought she was nice last year, but it's from two to three that she has really thrived. Her work in the spring really surprised us, she's been working really smartly. We expected her to win her maiden but it was hard next time giving away weight to some nice colts. We were very sweet coming into today ? her work has been pretty good. We were going to run her in a Listed race at Bath at the weekend but the ground was a bit quick so we decided to wait for today. I will be speak to Mr (Jaber) Abdullah (owner) but I'm sure black type will be on the horizon although I wouldn't mind taking in a nice handicap at Royal Ascot beforehand - Jack Channon, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: She's owned by Jaber Abdullah and won first time out at ­Windsor last August before ­finishing third at ­Goodwood on her ­second novice start. She really ­improved over the winter and won first time out at ­Wolverhampton over 5f last week. She'll be ­running over sprint ­distances this year. 02-04-25

entries.raceInstanceTitle: Al Basti Equiworld, Dubai July Cup Stakes (Group 1)

quotes.notes: Quinault is an absolute superstar. He's got an amazing will to win and if it's close, he just wants it - Stuart Williams, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Al Basti Equiworld Dubai Criterion Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.notes: Quinault is a fast horse and on his dam's side, he's definitely bred to go a bit further. Tom [Morley, joint-owner] continually have this argument whether he's best over a stiff six furlongs or an easy seven, but I think it's probably either. He's just a high-class horse who loves to win. Once he gets in front and rolling along at a place like this, he's hard to catch. We'd like to come back here to the Ebor meeting in August as it was a win and you're in race for it. We'll aim for that and be working back from there. He tries very hard and that's the key to it. It's his first Group win and it means a lot. I took him to Dubai in the winter and ran him in a Group 1, as we've always thought he was capable of this sort of thing - Stuart Williams, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Starman At Tally Ho Stud Garrowby Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.notes: We thought Quinault wouldn't like this ground but he just wants to win - he definitely tries. He's a special horse for a yard the size of ours, especially as he came a long way in such a short space of time last year. He had a little wobble earlier this year and was a little bit ill after we gave him the flu jab, but he's bang in form now. He's such a special horse. There's a chance he improves again next year and I still think he might be better over seven furlongs, so we've got to explore that avenue as well. He'll have a little bit of a break now as he's done his bit for the summer, but we could travel with him. He's a gelding so we'll go where the best prize-money is that he can win. There isn't much point in running him in Group races just for the sake of it - Stuart Williams, trainer.
I don't think Quinault was in love with the ground but he just tries very hard - Stuart Williams, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Liverpool Airport Faster, Easier, Friendlier Queensferry Stakes (Listed)
quotes.notes: I'd love Quinault to go seven furlongs round a bend somewhere if I could find the right race for him - I think that would be ideal. We wouldn't be against travelling him later in the year. We might go abroad somewhere, some of the tighter tracks, maybe in America, somewhere like that might suit him - Stuart Williams, trainer.

What a special horse Quinault has been for everybody this year. He didn't run a bad race the last day but he's back on song today - it's a special day. He's got one way of running in that you let him stride on in front, and he's so genuine he keeps finding for you - Luke Catton, jockey.

We had Sendintank who won ten handicaps in a season, including four in a week twice, but that was at a much lower level than this - this is very different. Quinault is a very tough horse and he's got loads of talent as well. Luke Catton has done a fantastic job settling him and it's such a shame he cannot do the weight. The horse was just a runaway when he arrived, he would just bolt. We trained him on a treadmill for the first two months so he never left the yard, before we slowly started to introduce him to the Heath, so there's a lot of work gone into what you're seeing today. He's always had the talent, it's just been a case of letting the horse know it and letting him use it - he's always been fast, that wasn't the problem! He's bred to get further so as long as we can keep him settled in his races that's a route we'll look to go with him - Stuart Williams, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Oakmere Homes Supporting Macmillan Sprint Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
quotes.notes: This was the biggest occasion Quinault has been to and he got a little bit warm in the preliminaries but he settled nicely in the race and Connor gave him a lovely ride, just managing to get him there on the line. We put him in at Ascot just in case something happened that forced our hand, but my gut feeling is probably not to run. I think he'll get a bit further and I've put him in the Bunbury Cup so that's a possibility - Stuart Williams, trainer.

It was unfortunate Luke Catton couldn't ride Quinault today as he couldn't do the weight. Luke has done a brilliant job settling him at home as he was a tearaway when he came but that is why Godolphin put him in the sale in the first place. He will probably go to York now for the valuable three-year-old six-furlong handicap as long as he comes out of this fine - Stuart Williams, trainer.

entries.raceInstanceTitle: Dubai Duty Free Irish Derby (Group 1) (No Geldings)

quotes.notes: Raaheeb behaved well at Ascot and that was out of character for him [giving trouble before the start]. Hopefully it was just a bit of freshness first time. He got his mind on the job in the race and I thought he was very professional. Rossa [Ryan] said he picked up twice and I couldn't fault him in the race. I thought he hit the line strong and I'm sure he'll sharpen up a bit for racing and I'd have no qualms about him getting a bit further. He's in the Dante but we always felt the Derby might come a fraction too soon for him mentally. He's pleasantly surprised me there but we'll have to see how he comes out of this and I wouldn't want to commit either way at the moment - Owen Burrows, trainer.Raaheeb is a lovely horse. He jumped well, settled good and I had the opportunity to slip off the rail as we were turning in just to get him rolling early. His work at home has been good and physically he's all there but he's just not clocked it mentally yet and he's just figuring it all out. I shouldn't think a mile and a half will be a problem. His pedigree says it shouldn't and he felt that way, as though the extra two furlongs wouldn't bother him. It's just whether he's ready for it mentally with the Derby being early enough in the season - Rossa Ryan, jockey, speaking on Racing TV.

quotes.raceTitle: Charbonnel et Walker British EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.notes: He's got a very laid-back attitude and I thought from that draw in stall 1 Raaheeb was very professional. He got a lot of cover but he travelled well and went through the race very pleasingly. Nothing's going to quicken in this ground too much because Jim [Crowley] said it's pretty soft, but he lengthened and went up through and hit the line strongly. He's a miler now, and I think he'll be a mile-and-a-quarter, mile-and-a-half horse next year. He's only been on the grass once but he's done everything pleasingly at home, with a very laid-back attitude. Once he switches on he'll be better, Jim said going under the tunnel there he tripped twice because he was half asleep, but that's a good way to have them at this stage. We'll see how he comes out of it. Whatever we can get from him this year is just going to be a bonus, so we won't go too mad - Owen Burrows, trainer.The Royal Lodge would be straight into deeper territory. I'd have loved to have gone for the Haynes, Hanson & Clark Stakes but that's even quicker and that's a no-no. There's possibly the Somerville Tattersall Stakes [on September 25] but we'll just go gently with Raaheeb. He's a big, raw horse and it's more about the future. It's just lovely to see he's got the ability to do that first time - Angus Gold, Shadwell racing manager.

entries.raceInstanceTitle: Qatar Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe (Group 1) (3yo+ No Geldings) (Grande Course) (Turf)

quotes.notes: Rahiebb has really matured physically over the winter. You only had to look at him in the paddock. You wouldn't have to know anything about horses to know that he's a magnificent specimen, a gorgeous horse. Hopefully his best days are ahead of him because he's a classic, late-maturing, staying horse. We've got to think he's a Cup horse. It's a tough division but a fun division to be involved in. He's a classy horse with stamina. I just hope he's maturing into himself mentally as well as physically - Roger Varian, trainer.It's my first year riding as first jockey to Roger [Varian] and we had high hopes for the season with Rahiebb. Today was going to be a 'where do we go with him?' moment. I knew turning in I was going well, I just didn't want to get there too early but he galloped out strongly. The feel he gave me there was completely different to the Leger, he stays well but obviously has gears and he's very exciting - Ray Dawson, jockey.

I'm proud and delighted with Rahiebb but gutted to be honest though. Watching it I thought most of the way round he was going to run well and finish strong. With a furlong to run I thought he'd get there but congratulations to the winner, he's a very good horse. I'm proud of ours and I think he's got a big future. He took a while to come to hand and even in his very good run at Royal Ascot in the Vase he did most things wrong that day. He was still learning on the job today. I have to give a shout out to Tony Procter who rides him out every day at home, he's not always easy. He's a lovely horse and I'm looking forward to him next year. I'd have thought that would be it for the year, he got going in February and didn't race as a two-year-old, he's all about next year - Roger Varian, trainer.

Rahiebb has run a really good race, he's a very nice horse. A horse to look forward to, hopefully for the next year or two in that staying division. He's still a baby, he didn't behave great in the prelims, just showing a bit of immaturity. He was slow from the gates, the draw didn't take his chance away, but made it difficult. He hasn't quite got a clear passage, he didn't really get stopped, but he didn't quite get an open runway. I still thought he would win with two to run. Then he was sort of wandering off a straight line, I don't know if it was greenness or ground, hot day, used a bit of nervous energy before the race. I think when you throw everything into the mix, he's a nice horse who performed very well, a bit frustrating we didn't quite bring it home, but a nice one for the future - Roger Varian, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He gave Merchant 8lb and was beaten only two and a half lengths in a handicap last May, and I think he was the best horse in the Queen's Vase on his next start. He was green and a thug beforehand - he just didn't behave or run like a professional, but was still beaten only a length. He looked like winning the St Leger in the final furlong on his last start, but he couldn't quite get past Scandinavia. That was a very good run and I think staying is his game. You'd have to dream that he'd be a Gold Cup horse with a run or two before. He might start in the Sagaro at Ascot, but it's not completely set in stone. He's a likeable thug and is looking super. 01-04-26

We were quite hopeful of a good run from him in the Leger. I know it's easy in hindsight, but I think people are very short-sighted when they're looking at a horse's chance. A lot of people don't go back past their last run. Even looking at the handicap at York in May, he gave Merchant 8lb and got beaten two and a half lengths. Merchant has since won the King George V Handicap at Royal Ascot and the Gordon Stakes at Glorious Goodwood. Even at the weights that was a good effort, and then in the Queen's Vase at Ascot it was a hell of a run. He did a lot wrong that day but was beaten only a length by Paddy Twomey's Carmers, who was 4-1 for the St Leger. I was pretty confident we had him in good shape for the Leger and we were vindicated by keeping the faith in him. There might have been only seven runners but the winner was admirable and I think it was a strong Leger, with the Derby winner in fourth. He arguably delivered a Group 1 performance when runner-up, without quite winning the prize, and it gives us a taste for what is maybe to come next year. We'll be unlikely to see him again this season. His season started early as his first run was in early March. He's had a very long year, although he's had only two races since Royal Ascot. He's all about next year now. I think he's going to be more of a Cup horse than a middle-distance horse and it'll be exciting to have him in the team - it's always nice to have a strong stayer. We hope he might be a horse to have around for another couple of years. The programme for Cup horses is interesting before Ascot, but after Ascot there's a lovely run of staying races, so we have a lot to look forward to with him. 24-09-25

quotes.notes: I'm pleased to get her back over 1,000 metres [five furlongs] because the race in Dubai really showed me that Rayevka doesn't stay further. We gave her a little bit of time when she came back and that went about as well as a comeback can go. The Group 1 at Royal Ascot is her objective and before that there is a Group 3 at Chantilly on Jockey Club day [the Prix du Gros-Chene] and, depending on how she is physically, we'll see if she needs to run there or go straight to Ascot. Mickael [Barzalona] told me she was pretty ready to run today, so we might well skip Chantilly and go straight to Ascot  - Francis Graffard, trainer.

This is a filly we needed to switch off - we have no choice, Rayevka is still learning how to race. Mickael [Barzalona] took the ride clean; unfortunately we didn't have one to take her a little bit further, but she picked up very nicely and it is a very good performance to be third in this race. She's entered in the Prix Maurice de Gheest; she's a very nice sprinting filly - I have to see. She will definitely stay at this sort of trip, though. She might be able to do seven furlongs but she will have to switch off. I always liked her - I took her to the Cheveley Park last season because I always thought she was a talented filly, but mentally she was not ready. Her last run we decided to change tactics completely and drop her in behind and see what she could do, and she was very convincing that day. I still liked her so we came here, and I think it was worth it - Francis Graffard, trainer.

Rayevka has always worked like a very good filly but in her comeback run this year she pulled too hard and today the idea was to get her to drop the bit early on. She's a sprinter with a late turn of foot and it's great to see her confirm in the afternoon what she shows in the morning. Mickael Barzalona said he could have made all on her but we wanted her to learn something. She isn't entered in the Commonwealth Cup, so we'll have to have a think about what we do - Nemone Routh, Aga Khan Studs racing manager.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: She's under consideration to be supplemented for the Commonwealth Cup. She's taken her race at Chantilly very well and there aren't that many opportunities to run against her own age group. She's always been a very smart worker and she's a sprinter who can really accelerate. She's a very solid sprint-built filly but she must have good ground. We were very happy with her in the Prix Marchand d'Or because she pinged out of the stalls and then Mickael [Barzalona] managed to get her some cover and she dropped the bit. She could do well if she runs that way again.  11-06-25

quotes.notes: We'll discuss it with Princess Zahra, but I would have thought we'll go to the St James's Palace Stakes at Ascot? I don't really want to step Rayif up in trip. We were lucky to have a good draw and Mickael [Barzalona] was able to ride him close to the pace, and he's a colt who always gets to a high cruising speed quickly. He had a great trip and was in the perfect spot to launch his attack. It was a wonderful victory - Francis Graffard, trainer.I wasn't sure Rayif would stay the distance, but Francis [Graffard] thought he would. He did so very well. I imagine it wasn't heavy ground as it'd only been raining for a couple of hours. He certainly had the speed to get through it. Mickael had the most amazing timing, it was lovely to see. I think he'll remain at a mile - Princess Zahra Aga Khan, owner, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

Hopefully, she'll fill all of her potential in the next 12 months and is a filly to look forward to. I think she can get a mile and a half, no problem - Ger Lyons, trainer.

quotes.notes: Regional was as big as a house in the parade ring and he took a blow at the furlong-pole then stuck his head out. He hit the line well. He'll go straight to Ascot for the six-furlong race - Ed Bethell, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: King Charles III Stakes (Group 1) (British Champions Series)
quotes.notes: Another half-a-furlong and we might have got there but that's horseracing. We can be nothing but proud of Regional. I would imagine we will try and aim towards something like the July Cup now - Ed Bethell, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Betfair Sprint Cup Stakes (Group 1) (British Champions Series)
quotes.notes: It was a massive performance. It looked smooth and Regional was one of the last to come off the bridle. In the Nunthorpe, he was rushed off his feet but he was so much more comfortable at this trip and I'm over the moon for everyone. The owners might want to go to America but I'll see how the horse is first and then we'll make a decision - Ed Bethell, trainer.

Fast ground and flat tracks are his big things and we'll try and keep Regional to that now. I'd imagine we'll look at the Nunthorpe in August as it looks a logical target. We'll chat about what we do in the interim - there's the City Walls with a penalty or the King George at Goodwood. He wasn't the same horse last season as he is this year, he's just thrived and is enjoying his races - Ed Bethell, trainer.

I wasn't expecting to make the running, but Regional is a decent horse and always has been. He came third in a Stewards' Cup and was unlucky in other handicaps, so I'm delighted for him. He ran off 100 in the Stewards' Cup and I think that's his mark in handicaps, which might make life difficult, but there's the City Walls back here now he's shown he's electric. I didn't think he was and he's shown me he's quick enough - Ed Bethell, trainer.

We thought we'd have to pay 30,000 and we paid 3,500gns and I'm not sure why. Regional's work had been good at home before and we were hopeful but I was a little unsure whether he'd strip fit enough for today. He's got a nice future, that's for sure, I'm looking forward to him - Ed Bethell, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: British Stallion Studs EBF Maiden Stakes
quotes.notes: Regional travelled well and was very professional - Tony Hamilton, jockey.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He's exciting. I was delighted with him in Ireland, the stiff 6f at the Curragh probably isn't his bag, so he'll go for the King Charles and I hope he'll run well over the stiff 5f at Ascot. He's come out of the race well and he's got a chance, but it's only a chance. It's going to be a tough gig. 10-06-24

He's a legend and must be one of the most consistent sprinters around. He never runs a bad race in a Group 1 - he hasn't been out of the first three at the top level apart from in the Nunthorpe once. He ran well at Ascot, but the older he's getting the more distance he probably wants so we'll take him up to six furlongs and look at the Prix Maurice de Gheest at Deauville and then go back to the Sprint Cup at Haydock. He's as good as ever at seven. He hasn't been overraced and the owners are reaping the rewards. He's taken us all on a journey none of us could ever believe he would. We're very lucky to have him. 02-07-25

quotes.notes: Rogue Lightning ran a great race He was always up there and led in the straight but was just run out of it. He's lost nothing in defeat and I feel we'll leave him out there to run in another Grade 2 sprint at Churchill Downs over Kentucky Derby weekend [May 3]. If you look at it another way, he would have had to carry a penalty in that if he'd won at Keeneland, so it could work in our favour - Tom Clover, trainer.
That was marvellous. Mickael [Barzalona, jockey] did well to drop Rogue Lightning out early from his draw and everything went well. He came through the horses smoothly - Tom Clover, trainer.
We put Rogue Lightning in the Abbaye and if he's okay we'll go there. I've always really liked him and he's very fast - Tom Clover, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Dash (Handicap)
quotes.notes: Rogue Lightning is a really nice horse and it was very sporting of the owners to come to a race like this. I think we'll perhaps look at something like the Scarborough Stakes at Doncaster next. He won well there last time and hopefully looks like he's worth a crack at stakes company now. He showed plenty of talent as a 2yo but bringing him back to 5f with a hood has really helped and he's relaxed and grown up - Tom Clover, trainer.

Gelding him, applying the hood and and the drop back to five furlongs seems to have helped him just relax a bit. Carrie Browning rides him every day and she also rides Rogue Millennium. She's got him back fit and deserves a lot of the credit. Rogue Lightning has always been a horse with lots of ability and it's nice to see him show some of his full potential today - Tom Clover, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He got back from America last week. It was great for him to win in Qatar given his connections and then he ran a huge race at Keeneland. It didn't work out for us at Churchill Downs last time. He was caught wide and they'd had a lot of rain, so he had a bit of wheelspin and it was really hard to make up ground there. We need to put a line through it and go again. I want to enter him in the July Cup. I feel like 6f is what he wants now and hopefully he can still fly the flag for us this year. 14-05-25

quotes.notes: We were pretty confident coming here. Rolltight had a very good run the first day. We thought he'd be a bit more streetwise today. He's in the big race, the Classic (at Gowran on June 1). We'll see how he is. Maybe a little close but if he comes out of it well and, I'll speak to the owners, that might be his next shot - Johnny Murtagh, trainer.

Roman Dragon is so special around here. He loses interest in a straight line a lot of the time, he looks at the crowd and whatever, and he's a very balanced, agile, nimble horse. He'll come back here when he can, the problem is the better he gets the fewer races there are. He won the Queensferry last year and we'll try and win it again - Hugo Palmer, trainer.

Roman Dragon is an absolute star and it was a first-class ride by Jason [Watson]. He read the race supremely well, but the horse was very tough. Turning in I thought we were going to win by even further as we were going so well. He loves it here and he's a sprint handicapper who pulled it out of the bag in a stakes race. I'm not sure he can go to a much higher level than this, but he's turned his love for this track into a massive advantage. He goes so well here and that's worth half a dozen pounds ? it was probably the difference today. Chester made a nice rug for him and he's a history maker - Hugo Palmer, trainer.

Roman Dragon loves Chester. That's now six wins here for this horse, which has equalled the modern-day track record. We had a nice enough draw [five] and everything went perfectly - Hugo Palmer, trainer.

Nick (Hughes, part-owner)'s ambition is for Roman Dragon to become the winningmost horse around Chester and we think he needs six. We're two-thirds of the way there. I'm delighted, he won off 84 last year and 79 here so maybe we can get another before the season's out - Hugo Palmer, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He's such a star and has had two good winters in Bahrain. He has a higher rating than he's ever won off, although he did come agonisingly close a couple of times last summer, but I don't think winning off this mark is out of the question. He loves Chester and will go to the May meeting. 09-04-25

He's just an absolute joy. He's the winningmost horse at Chester after two more wins there this season. He's that lucky individual who hasn't seen an English winter for a few years and he's heading back to Bahrain. The handicapper dropped him a couple of pounds for a below-par effort on very soft ground in the Portland, which means he'll get a run or two before he has to step up in grade out there. He's had three fantastic winters there now - he was the series winner this year having been second last year. He's that rare thing - a racehorse who pays for himself. 08-10-25

quotes.notes: There's a Listed race at Newcastle next week [Golden Rose Stakes], but I thought they could go very steady there and then sprint, which wouldn't have suited Room Service, so we took a punt here. He's lightly raced and had a bit of a wind issue that we corrected, but he's still quite a raw horse. Whether he wanted it this soft was another thing too, but he's a very good horse. He's crying out for another furlong too and he proved that at York last time and here. You'd imagine he'll do plenty strength-wise as we know he's got the engine - Kevin Ryan, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Northern Commercials Iveco E-Daily, Zero Emissions Handicap
quotes.notes: Room Service ran in the Greenham and didn't quite get 7f and he ran a cracker in Listed company there last time. This fast pace and stiff finish suited him down to the ground - Adam Ryan, assistant trainer.

After York I thought this extra half furlong would definitely suit Room Service. And we were very hopeful he'd go on the ground. He's been maturing all year. We've been taking it steady with him and it's paying off now. Whether we run him again this year I don't know but I'd say he'll get a mile well next year - Kevin Ryan, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: All he did was progress last season and he ended up winning the big sales race at Doncaster. He surprised me how well he went through the soft ground that day because he's got the action of a fast-ground horse. He even ran green when he hit the front and you'd be very hopeful he can progress again this season. He missed the Burradon Stakes at Newcastle on Good Friday and is heading for either the Craven Stakes, a 7f conditions race at Newmarket or the Greenham at Newbury. He's got an entry in the Irish 2,000 Guineas and his comeback will determine which route we take. 04-04-24

quotes.raceTitle: Arqana Series des Pouliches (Conditions) (Unraced 2yo Fillies) (Straight Course) (Turf)
quotes.notes: When Richard [Hughes, trainer] bought her and the incentive was there, he always said this was the race he was going to target. The prize-money is fantastic and we're absolutely thrilled. Rose Ghaiyyath had a couple of away days and Richard was always very happy with her, and he has some big plans for her. But this was always where he wanted to start off - David Ryan, owner's representative.

quotes.notes: Rosy Affair has done really well for a little bit of a winter break. She had to do the donkey work on the front end at Newmarket which probably wasn't ideal first run back. I managed to get a tow today and she was pretty straightforward from there. She ran on similar ground in France last year so I wasn't too worried about it, albeit I do think she's better on a quicker surface. I imagine she'll have some loftier targets but she's done everything right and I loved the way she's really growing up. She was quite hot for her last couple of years but George [Boughey] and the team have done a really good job of getting her to relax - Billy Loughnane, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: She performed much better in the second half of last year and we toyed with the idea of the Al Quoz Sprint in Dubai but decided to be patient. It was no surprise when she won a Group 3 in August and she's going to work back from midsummer targets. We'd love to get her to Royal Ascot and I'd imagine she'll start in a Listed race. 02-04-26

quotes.raceTitle: Sky Bet Lowther Stakes (Group 2) (Fillies) (IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.notes: We've always thought a lot of Royal Fixation. She ran a huge race at Newmarket and it's been a really long six weeks. You let her down and built her back up and hope you've got it right and haven't left her too fresh. It's been quite a challenge. What's exciting is that she still looked a bit green off the bridle. I think she'll go for the Cheveley Park Stakes. She's quick and is from a very fast female line - Ed Walker, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Duchess Of Cambridge Stakes (Sponsored By bet365) (Group 2) (Fillies)
quotes.notes: I'm very proud of her. When you come into this on the back of winning a Thirsk maiden you don't really know how good you are, but Royal Fixation is very good. It would have been disappointing had she run badly as we rate her very highly among our two-year-olds. To run that filly as close as we did is pretty exciting, as I think the winner is a very special filly. The Lowther would have to be an option - Ed Walker, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Join BresBet EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.notes: Royal Fixation did things quite effortlessly through the first half of the race, and I thought she finished off her race well. She seemed a little bit too classy for the rest of them - George Downing, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: Last year's Lowther winner and a very quick filly. She's quite relaxed and we were considering going for a Guineas trial, but I think she's a sprinter as her pedigree is all speed. We'll go for one of the Commonwealth Cup trials instead. 31-03-26

quotes.raceTitle: Virgin Bet Daily Extra Places Doonside Cup Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.notes: I always had tabs on the leader and I thought we went a nice gallop. I was just trying to get Royal Rhyme to relax and he was in great form and very professional. He won very nicely the last day at Goodwood and definitely deserves to be at this level. I felt like we were going a good gallop and he picked up and kept going off it and hit the line strong. The ground has dried up a little from yesterday and it's a bit tacky as well. This lad likes this sort of ground, so it's worked out well - Clifford Lee, jockey.

I think Royal Rhyme is definitely a Listed class and possibly Group horse in the making. This is his kind of trip. He probably would get further if he learns to relax, but for now, definitely a mile and a quarter. He loves this type of ground - Clifford Lee, rider.

When I rode Royal Rhyme at Kempton, early doors all he did was gallop away. The extra couple of furlongs though has done him justice. He travels well through that sort of ground and he's done it nicely now. I feel like he'll get a bit further as he's a very strong-travelling horse - Clifford Lee, jockey.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: I'm convinced he can nick a Group 1 on very soft ground. He's run well in two Champion Stakes and just got a little niggle after his last run and we had to back off him, but he looks in great shape and is moving well. He could start off in the Brigadier Gerard, which he won two years ago, or go to Ireland. I'd imagine the autumn will be when he gets his optimum conditions. 31-03-26

quotes.notes: Royal Zabeel has enjoyed the faster ground here than it was at Haydock last time. We'll leave it to the brains trust to decide where he goes next - Ronnie Whelan, syndicate member.
Alistair [Rawlinson] rode a cool race and got Royal Zabeel in a good position early to strike off the home turn - Chris Dixon, owner's representative.

quotes.raceTitle: Jayne - On Course Lady Bookmaker EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race) (Div I)
quotes.notes: That was very pleasing. I thought Royal Zabeel had a good run here first time, he was a bit unlucky as he had a bad passage round. He had a nice draw today and Ryan kept it very uncomplicated. He's gone round there with his ears pricked and he'll have learned an awful lot again. Ryan said don't rush him back so we'll give him a bit of time, let him get over it. He's a horse we've liked all along - Kevin Ryan, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He won his maiden well at Pontefract but was probably wanting a break when he disappointed in the Flying Scotsman on his next start. He's ready to start off as soon as we get some nice ground, probably over 6f. We like him a lot and we'll see how far he can progress this season. 04-04-24

We bought him out of James Tate's stable where he had one run, having previously been with Kevin Ryan. He was a very easy winner of a Pontefract maiden as a two-year-old, after which he was highly tried. He's had only five starts, so he hasn't had much racing at all. We liked his run at Pontefract just before the sales when he was third in a race full of hardened handicappers. He's a big, strong, good-looking horse with a pedigree to suggest he'll train on well. He's been gelded and he'll have plenty of time to come to himself. 26-09-24

quotes.raceTitle: Coral Charge (Group 3) (Registered As The Sprint Stakes)
quotes.notes: It's fantastic to see Rumstar get his head back in front. Like for any sprinter, everything needs to go just right on the day. I don't think he liked Haydock and at Royal Ascot he got in front a bit too soon. He was also drawn wide and it just didn't work out for him. We made a conscious decision to hang on to him today come through. That is very risky at Sandown as you often don't get that run and meet traffic but Rob [Hornby] found thar gap and rode him to perfection. He knows the horse well and loves him as much as I do. We deliberately didn't entered in the King George at Goodwood as I just though five furlongs there in that Grade might be a bit sharp for him. I am not sure where we will go next. We may have to step up to six furlongs where there are more options although I would prefer to stay at five - Jonathan Portman, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Hong Kong Jockey Club World Pool Palace House Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.notes: We have been very much looking forward to running Rumstar. It seems to have been a long time since last October, waiting for him to get back on the track. He has been in fantastic form and looking great this year. It's great to be back and great to have him back winning in this company. I think we had him where we wanted him today and I think he is a stronger horse this year. I don't weight my horses but he seems heavier than he was last year and the year before - Jonathan Portman, trainer.

I'm just delighted I've found a race for Rumstar to win because it's been a long time since the Cornwallis. He's not been the luckiest and had a few training issues last year. I was concerned about the ground, but that was obviously a load of rubbish! I'm chuffed for the horse and chuffed for his owner Vincent Ward, who is sitting at home not very well - Jonathan Portman, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Coral Beaten-By-A-Length Free Bet Nursery Handicap
quotes.notes: Rumstar had been running well in Listed company and I take exception to anyone saying he came up short and was banging his head. He could go back for a Listed race, although there are no firm plans. He's not just a two-year-old - Jonathan Portman, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: At the beginning of the year the Nunthorpe was a race we never had in mind; we thought if we'd go for any Group 1 it would be the Prix de l'Abbaye, which he's entered for. But there are very few options for him at the moment and he seems extremely well, so we're probably going to take a leap of faith and run him at York. Everyone else seems to be doing it, so we thought we'd do it too. I don't think anyone's won a Group 1 staying at home. People say it's a very open year for sprinters and that there's no standout. But, however open they are, Group 1s are still very hard to win and we're under no illusions that dabbling in such company isn't necessarily his gig. 20-08-25

quotes.notes: Run Boy Run ran really well in the Portland the other day and we decided to rock and roll. We thought we were drawn on the wrong side but he's very fast and George gave him a great ride - Richard Spencer, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: BetUK. Home Of The Acca Restricted Maiden Stakes (For horses In Bands B, C And D) (GBB Race)
quotes.notes: Run Boy Run made very hard work of it. I wasn't overly keen on his attitude to be honest but I think some headgear will iron that out - Jason Hart, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.notes: It was brilliant. I wouldn't want to be rude, but it wasn't the greatest race. Run To Freedom rating said he should be there or thereabouts, and he has just been in good form lately. It's a great tale. Godfrey (Wilson) who owns him - it's his last horse and he has been very keen to go on with him. I kept telling him there is no way this horse is going to win Group races, as an eight-year-old entire! Godfrey, quite rightly, didn't listen and has had a wonderful day today. He has been second in Group Ones but can be a bit naughty as he can hold a bit back for himself sometimes, as you would expect from an eight-year-old who is still an entire. He was very genuine today and always racing well on the bridle. It looked like he was going to win from the start. It's wonderful for everyone at home. They've done a grand job - Henry Candy, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Al Basti Equiworld, Dubai July Cup Stakes (Group 1)
quotes.notes: Run To Freedom is an amazing horse. When he's absolutely on-song he's a really good horse and he loves a bit of an uphill finish. He's got some fantastic form in Group 1 races, it would be lovely if we could just nick one somewhere. He doesn't like firm ground but he's coping with it now he's older. Firm ground and the draw didn't help him greatly at Ascot but he still finished a neck behind Inisherin, so I don't think he really deserved to be that price. You can never write him off but you could never tip him - Henry Candy, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Pertemps Network July Cup Stakes (Group 1) (British Champions Series)
quotes.notes: Run To Freedom is a very able horse and we knew he could do that, he showed it at Salisbury and when second behind Kinross in the Champions Sprint last year. You can never quite rely on him, which is why he starts at these ridiculous prices, but the ability is there. I wouldn't be surprised if he was able to win one before the end of the year. We'll go to Haydock and we'll go to Ascot in October - Henry Candy, trainer.
Hopefully getting his head back in front will spark a revival in Run To Freedom, who looked like he was going to be a world beater as a two-year-old - Henry Candy, trainer.
Russet Gold is a classy horse, a half-brother to Daahyeh who I won the Albany on. He'll stay six furlongs but his quality got him through the race - David Egan, jockey.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: There's no reason to think he won't keep improving with age and I'd love to place him to win a Listed race. He should be ready to start in the second half of May. 11-04-25

quotes.raceTitle: Book The Ladbrokes Ayr Gold Cup Handicap (GBBplus Race)
quotes.notes: Ryka travelled okay. I don't think she was enjoying the ground that much, but she's got a nice attitude and gives her all. My head was down on the line so I had every chance - Danny Tudhope, rider, speaking to Racing TV.

quotes.raceTitle: Sky Bet Go-Racing-In-Yorkshire Summer Festival EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.notes: It's a nice starting place and we thought Ryka would run well, but she'll probably need further. She's done that really nicely, she's green as grass and will definitely come on a ton for it - Stewart Tosh, representing owners Akela Thoroughbreds.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: She won her debut on fast ground and then we pitched her into two stakes races on soft, but she didn't show up. We'll up her in trip on better ground as she has plenty of stamina in her family. She'll start off in handicaps with a view to going back into black-type races. 14-04-25

quotes.notes: Saba Desert is a horse we liked from the get-go and were pleased with the way he did it at Sandown. He progressed from Sandown to here and we always try and find one for this race. He is a lovely deep-girthed horse and we'll work back from a Dewhurst now. Whether we go the National Stakes or go to the Champagne and then the Dewhurst - we'll see. He'll have a bit of a break now as he has a Group Two penalty - Charlie Appleby, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: British Stallion Studs EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.notes: When you ask for Saba Desert, he's there immediately ? he's a very talented colt - William Buick, jockey, speaking on Racing TV.
