quotes.notes: Saddadd was impressive. I was hopeful he'd run really strong today as he's had a good preparation. He has a great attitude, a really good way of going and he'd wintered well and he's worked super all spring. We wanted to learn today and get the direction for the year ahead and we weren't sure coming into this whether we'd be sticking at ten furlongs or going up to a mile and a half. He's a very relaxed horse and both are options, though I don't think we need to go a mile and a half just yet. He's in the Tattersalls Gold Cup, and I could see him enjoying the Curragh as a track, but does he need to tackle that just yet? We'd love to maybe come back here for the Eclipse, so it's about getting there. We could go to the Brigadier Gerard under a penalty or to Ireland  - Roger Varian, trainer.Saddadd is an absolute legend of a horse. There were question marks about whether we were going to run him over a mile and a half depending on how he ran today but he's actually got quicker. He puts himself in a race wherever you need him and he seems as though he's taken a step forward from last year. He's exciting - Ray Dawson, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

quotes.raceTitle: Read Meg Nicholls' Blog At betmgm.co.uk Handicap
quotes.notes: I've always really liked Saddadd is a beautiful animal, lovely to look at, and my five-year-old girl could take him down to the start - he's so relaxed. We always thought he wanted some dig in the ground. He's genuine and an exciting horse. I think he was trying to give it all but he was still learning on the way round, finding his balance around the bend on the soft ground. He's picked up well and I think on more suitable ground with a bit of dig, you'll see a better horse. It was an impressive win carrying a lot of weight - Ray Dawson, rider.

quotes.raceTitle: Trade Nation London Gold Cup Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
quotes.notes: Saddadd is a very laid back horse with a big heart. I think he'll keep improving but I do think he'll appreciate a bit more give in the ground when it comes. He's shown a lot of grit today. This race has a great history of producing Pattern performers and he might deserve a crack at something like the Hampton Court - Roger Varian, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Boost Your Acca At BetMGM EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (Div I)
quotes.notes: It was a lovely performance. I thought Saddadd would be a bit green early on, which he was jumping out and finding his stride, but I got into a nice rhythm, a nice sort of pocket to teach him a bit about having horses either side of him. He took a little bit of winding up, but once he did get into top gear, and I had the rail to just help me out a bit, the penny started to drop late on and he finished off good - Jack Mitchell, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: I really like him and he's a horse I expect to find a new level this season. I've got a feeling his best trip is going to be a mile and a half, and I'd quite like to start him off in the John Porter. The other option is to wait for the Gordon Richards. He prefers some cut in the ground and he's got every chance of being a good horse. We looked after him last season and he's got the physical stamp of a horse who should improve with age. 01-04-26

He's thriving and we're really happy with him. We're going to run him in the Foundation Stakes at Goodwood on Wednesday and that'll give us a guide as to what to do with him for the rest of the year. I've always loved him and I think in time he could be top drawer. He's got a great attitude. I think he's got the temperament for a good horse and he has the ability. He's my trainer's pick. 24-09-25

quotes.raceTitle: FanDuel Breeders' Cup Mile presented by PDJF (Grade 1) (3yo+) (Turf)
quotes.notes: Sahlan ran a good race. We got a bit outpaced down the backstretch but he picked up well and was never nearer than at the finish - Mickael Barzalona, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: Qatar Prix du Moulin de Longchamp (Group 1) (3yo+) (Grande Course) (Turf)
quotes.notes: Today was a big challenge. I said to His Highness Sheikh Joaan that I didn't have many options for Sahlan and that he was in very good form and he can quicken. It was a big gamble but I said if he was in the first five it would be fine, we have nothing to lose, and he believed in me and obviously it paid off really nicely today. There was a lack of options and I've always liked the horse. In the Poule d'Essai we had a lot of excuses and then he was sick when he was beaten in the Listed race. He won comfortably in the Group 3 last time. I don't think I'll run him again here on soft ground," he added. "I'll speak to the entourage but if he's well, why not go to the Breeders' Cup Mile? We'll probably keep him as a four-year-old - Francis Graffard, trainer.

I've always thought plenty of Sahlan but he's not been straightforward and was actually sick last time so he couldn't show that acceleration. We decided to ride him cold today and get him covered up on the inside. They went hard and he really showed his class. He has a real turn of foot when you get him to switch off and has a lot of quality. We'll have to see how he comes out of this race but the mile is his trip and, as long as the ground stays good, we might have a look at the Moulin, where he would have nothing to lose - Francis Graffard, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Arc Prix Maurice de Gheest (Group 1) (3yo+) (Straight Course) (Turf)
quotes.notes: Saint Lawrence has run an absolute stormer and I think if the pace had been stronger, he'd have nearly won. He's definitely improving and he's proved himself at Group 1 level; he's taken a big step up from winning a handicap at Ascot - Hollie Doyle, jockey.

Saint Lawrence has always shown us plenty at home, he's a very nice horse to have around and I'm just delighted to get the job done on first time of asking. I fancied all three of them, I made sure Hollie chose which one to ride so it wasn't my fault and she chose right! - Archie Watson, trainer.

It was probably trainer error as a two-year-old thinking as he is by Al Kazeem Saint Lawrence would be fine over seven furlongs. He is entered in the King's Stand. James (Doyle, jockey) said he can go five or six and we might look at the Leisure Stakes at Windsor which is an easy six in about two weeks' time - Roger Varian, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Denford Stakes (Listed Race) (Formerly The Washington Singer Stakes)
quotes.notes: Saint Lawrence has looked a nice one and was one of ours we nominated early on in the first week (to get in certain races). Although he's by Al Kazeem he'd shown up well in May on the gallops and we thought he could be a Chesham horse. He didn't go down that route, but wasn't disgraced in the Pat Eddery or Superlative, although those races probably didn't go his way. I'm not sure about plans. Andrea said he'd get a mile, but I don't think he necessarily has to next time. He's had five runs, so maybe one or two more this season and the Royal Lodge can favour experience. Now he's a Listed winner, we have to aim at Group 3s and Group 2s and there are no soft options so we'll see. He'll be better on better ground - Roger Varian, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He could run in the Abernant at the Craven meeting or we might wait for a valuable 6f handicap at the Guineas meeting. Although he's not a regular winner, his runs in the Palace House and King's Stand last season were really good. He's been gelded, which might help, and he could be a Wokingham horse. 06-04-23

He won at Listed level as a two-year-old and has progressed this season without adding to his two career wins. His best run was when second to Rohaan in the Pavilion Stakes at Ascot in April, which was a superb effort. I'm looking forward to campaigning him in the autumn and he should get his head in front again as he's pleasing us at home. 18-08-21

quotes.raceTitle: ARC Prix Maurice de Gheest - Fonds Europeen de l'Elevage (Group 1) (3yo+) (Straight Course) (Turf)
quotes.notes: This is the first time I've had Sajir at 100 per cent. He's always had some minor issues, but today he was in perfect condition. It's [the Foret] the obvious race for him, like his father - Andre Fabre, trainer.That was brilliant. He relaxed very well. I was a little bit behind but the speed was on and I tried not to get there too soon. Sajir has probably improved at least 7lb on any form he'd previously shown. He was in cruise control for most of the race. When I rode him at Newmarket he didn't win by far but maybe it wasn't his best track and then he was a bit upset in the stalls at Ascot. He felt exceptional throughout the race. He switched leads in the closing stages and powered to the line -  Oisin Murphy, jockey.

We've had our eyes set on trying to make a stallion of Sajir at some point and Oisin said he wouldn't be out of place in trying to go for the six-furlong race at Royal Ascot (Queen Elizabeth II Jubilee Stakes) next. If we want to make a stallion, that is maybe where we should aim but it will be decided by Prince Faisal (owner-breeder) and Andre. We could also look at York if we want to go over seven furlongs - we just need to convince Andre to leave Deauville alone! Prince Faisal is here and watched it from the stands. He had Remaat finish third in the Nell Gwyn yesterday and is delighted. He raced the sire Make Believe having bought him as a foal so it's very special for him and a nice start to the season. This horse started well last year but unfortunately got an abscess in his near hind, which kept opening up during the season. He just wasn't quite firing although he ran well each time. We were pleased how he went through the winter. After he won in France last month, we wanted to go for the Al Quoz but in the end just didn't think he was battle-hardened enough yet. Part of the thinking in coming here today was that it fits right and will hopefully will help to make a man of him. I am pleased we came here today - Ted Voute, owner's racing manager.

We were a little bit worried about the distance going in, but we ran out of options because the ground has not been great everywhere. We had to run to tell us where we go next. Sajir handled the five and a half furlongs quite well from a bad draw. He's in the French Guineas but whether that's a little bit too far, I don't know. He's from a fast family and I think we'll let the dust settle and see whether we go up to seven, or whether the Prince wants to try him at a mile with the option to drop back. I think that's his call really - Ted Voute, owner's racing and bloodstock manager.

quotes.notes: This was an easier set of rivals than last time and on less testing ground. I think Samangan is a good-ground horse who is becoming more mature, and Mickael [Barzalona, jockey] was very happy with him. If we stick at 1,200 metres [six furlongs] then the aim will be the Commonwealth Cup [at Royal Ascot], with the hope that he might stretch out to seven in the Prix Jean Prat. Physically he's a big, strong horse, and built for sprinting. His jockey felt he was much more business-like this time, and when he asked him to accelerate he did it easily - Francis Graffard, trainer.

quotes.notes: Samangan is still quite immature and I'm not sure he will be effective when the ground gets really soft. Mickael [Barzalona, jockey] said he is becoming more tractable in his races and that he could go back up in trip at some stage, but I don't think you'll see him again this year and I imagine he'll start off next season at this trip - Nemone Routh, owners' racing manager.

quotes.notes: Santorini Star is very genuine, liked the ground today and will improve for the race. She is from a family that improves with age and I'm just sick that I didn't put her in the Coronation Cup! You'd think she'd make the running, but she doesn't have to. She just puts her head down and wants to win. Horses like that are hard to find, and she's from a family that improves with age - I think Dreamloper [the winner's half-sister] didn't half improve when she was five, and so this filly could as well. Today was a good start to her season. She was second in a Group One last year over a mile and six and a half, and she proved today she is quick enough to win a Group Two at this level. I don't know about the quality of the race today, but she did it well enough. I suspect a supplementary entry for the Coronation Cup will now be discussed at length. It's always a good race and I wish I'd put her in - it would have saved all the aggro! I didn't miss the entry, I just decided against it so more fool me.  There are no penalties in the Hardwicke, I think, and Ascot is lovely for everyone, so that is another possibility, but a Group One is what we want - William Haggas, trainer.William [Haggas] was keen to come back to a mile and a half because he thought Santorini Star had almost stepped into herself and quickened up a bit more for it. She's versatile, tough and has class so it's a great start to 2026 - Tom Marquand, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

quotes.raceTitle: Qatar Prix de Royallieu (Group 1) (3yo+ Fillies & Mares) (Grande Course) (Turf)
quotes.notes: It was a super run and Santorini Star put her all into it. The ground was probably a bit sticky in the end to really go through to the line. The winner picked up really well and she was a gallant second - Tom Marquand, jockey.

Santorini Star comes off the bridle early and you really feel in trouble but she stays really well and is tough at the finish. She enjoyed that ground and she's really finding her mojo now. Her form plateaued and she had a little break and that's seemingly been the making of her ? ever since that she's been in ripping form. It was a big step up from a handicap win at York and she's an exciting filly - Tom Marquand, rider.

quotes.raceTitle: Solar/British EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.notes: Santorini Star is a well-bred filly who ran a nice debut at Southwell last time. She'll only get better stepping up in trip. She was still a bit green today and I'd like to think she's learnt a bit here and can take another step forward again - Adam Farragher, jockey.

quotes.notes: We went into the race with a lot of confidence, Satono Reve was feeling so well in himself. Unfortunately we bumped into a very good horse today. Halfway through I thought I had him done but he just had another kick - Joao Moreira, jockey.

quotes.notes: This was a big jump coming here off a novice win last year, and Saxon Street is very much learning on the job, but when William asked him, he picked up nicely.  He should stay a mile a half without a problem. We'll have to decide whether we go straight there or stay at a mile and a quarter next time. There's a lot of water to go under the bridge between now and the Derby but that was a nice performance for his first run of the year  - Thady Gosden, joint-trainer.

quotes.notes: Richard [Hughes, trainer] told me to be as confident as I can. Sayidah Dariyan relaxes brilliantly when she's in behind and conserves plenty of energy. She's got an electric turn of foot when you let her down. I'll leave that [possible future targets] to Richard and his team, but she's in great nick and is definitely a filly on the up. She's got the best mind. She yawns in the stalls, but as soon as the gates open, she's all business - Billy Loughnane, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

I wouldn't normally take on horses rated 110 when you're 92 but Sayidah Dariyan was working really well at home. She could come back here in two weeks [Chelmer Fillies' Stakes], but I wouldn't be mad about that, or go for the Carnarvon which would be spot on - Richard Hughes, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: I was thrilled with her run in the Carnarvon at Newbury. The winner Symbol Of Honour can't run in the Commonwealth Cup as he's a gelding, so you can discount him, and it was only her second run on grass. She can only improve and she'll go there with a little squeak. 10-06-25

We really fancied her at Windsor at the start of the month, but she stumbled over every one of those ridges and it was hard to get her on an even keel. I backed her up just over a week later because it was the ideal race over 6f at Lingfield on the all-weather. I didn't think she'd win like she did and she's gone up in her estimation at home. We might go to Dundalk on October 4 for a Listed race over 5f. 18-09-24

quotes.notes: I'm delighted. Scandinavia is one of those big Gold Cup horses, he relaxes, he cruises, and he's happy to wait and finds plenty. Ryan gave him a lovely ride and he just ended up getting there a little bit earlier than he wanted. This is the perfect race to bridge the gap [to Royal Ascot] and his training will get more serious as we go along. He had a lovely run in Navan and this was a lovely run too. The Gold Cup is an unusual race, you're never sure until you go past that two miles and two and a quarter miles. We always thought he could kick in at that level of race and he's a big, relaxed horse. He finds everything really easily, so you couldn't be happier - Aidan O'Brien, speaking to Racing TV.

quotes.raceTitle: BAR 1 Betting Vintage Crop Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.notes: Lovely, Ryan [Moore] was delighted with Scandinavia. He always went like a Cup horse and Ryan thought the same there. The plan is to go for the Saval Beg at Leopardstown before the [Ascot] Gold Cup - Aidan O'Brien, trainer

I'm delighted, Scandinavia is hardy and Tom gave him a great ride. He stays very well obviously, but we were a little bit worried when the ground went on the slow side. The better the ground, the better you'll see him. He has a beautiful temperament and he stays, but he'll probably have no problem coming back to a mile and a half as he has loads of gears. Every week he's getting better. He's in the Melbourne Cup and he has to get scanned to see whether he's eligible to go or not, but there's every chance the lads might want to go down there with him - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

We're delighted. This was Illinois's race, all was planned out, but when Ryan [Moore] said at Newmarket that Scandinavia felt very classy, it was the right thing to do to let them come and run the two of them together and see. Scandinavia looks a very classy stayer, he travelled very well through the race and Wayne [Lordan] gave him a beautiful ride. He was always a very smart horse. The lads actually backed him for the Derby very early in his career, he was considered a very good horse. He won his maiden over a mile and a quarter and Wayne was delighted with him at Ascot next time - he got trapped six wide but he still didn't lie down the whole way and came back at the line to try and win. He's a great stayer with a great mind, he's uncomplicated, and like we saw today he handled the ease in the ground well. You couldn't be more delighted with him really. You would imagine he looks a ready-made Leger horse. Lambourn didn't go to the King George, he is looking at the Voltigeur, and after that an Arc or the British or Irish Leger after that. Scandinavia doesn't have to run again before the Leger if he's going there, so all the options are there - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.Scandinavia has improved all year. He was stepping up to two miles today against the older horses. It's a tough task but I thought he stepped forward quite well. He was hanging onto a little bit even when he got there so I think there's plenty of improvement to come. Today was going to find out how smart he is and he's obviously a very smart stayer - Wayne Lordan, jockey.

I think the St Leger in England, or Ireland, would be targets and then hopefully Scandinavia can develop into a cup horse for next year. We can plot our way to those nice staying races for the rest of the year. We'll see how the horses perform over the festivals at Goodwood and York. He seems to have improved again since Ascot. Hopefully now we can have some fun with him over these longer distances - Paul Smith, co-owner.Scandinavia has been improving with every race and ran well at Ascot. He got into a lovely rhythm today and stayed on really well. I never rode him in a race before although I have rode him at home, so I wouldn't know about the [first-time] cheekpieces. He was impressive today - Ryan Moore, jockey.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He won two Group 1 races last season, the Goodwood Cup followed by the St Leger. He'll be going down the staying route again. He's a big, long-striding horse and we're very happy with everything he's doing. He'll more than likely go for the Vintage Crop and the Saval Beg. 31-03-26

quotes.notes: Oisin [Murphy] got off her and said she's an absolute machine. He said he felt like he was going to win all the way. We're delighted. See The Fire won the race last year very impressively but you never know if she's going to come back and do it again. But she'd been doing some lovely work at home - Anna Lisa Balding, trainer's wife.

quotes.raceTitle: British Stallion Studs EBF Nottinghamshire Oaks Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies & Mares)
quotes.notes: It was always going to be a muddling race and it was my own fault, really. See The Fire moved through the race with ease and we saw plenty of the front, which is never ideal. She's very game, but just needed a bit of company - Rob Hornby, jockey.

It's another Group 1 place and See The Fire is just a lovely racemare. That should set her up perfectly for the Nassau, which was always her main target - Andrew Balding, trainer.Career best. Race set up for a closer, it was an end-to-end gallop. Good run - Oisin Murphy, rider of See The Fire.

quotes.raceTitle: Al Basti Equiworld Dubai Middleton Fillies' Stakes (Group 2)
quotes.notes: We've always had a very high opinion of See The Fire and she's improved since last year. We were a little disappointed with her run at Sandown but she probably needed it as she travelled well but didn't quite get home, that probably put her spot on for today. She's a very exciting horse. We always fancied going back for the Nassau as she was second in it last year and that's the primary objective. If that goes well we might consider coming back here in August. We made a bit of a b******s of campaigning her last year when not stepping up in trip until it was too late. She obviously relishes this trip. She really found her feet after her Eclipse run last year and ran really well on Champions Day, having had a busy season. There's lots of look forward to - Andrew Balding, trainer.

See The Fire was very good at Goodwood and deserved to win a decent race. Hopefully she'll now go on to better things. We don't need to remind people who her dam was when winning the Juddmonte, so we know she was bred for the job. She actually likes not having space, although she's not overly-big. She enjoys tracking on to the back of them like she did at Goodwood, but then when it opened up she was electric. I'd definitely say we'll be going for a Group 1 next - Oisin Murphy, rider.

quotes.raceTitle: Qatar Nassau Stakes (Group 1) (Fillies & Mares) (British Champions Series)
quotes.notes: It was a good run from See The Fire. I thought it was a pace collapse from two furlongs out and I felt I'd pick up Ryan, but as he taught me in the last race, he takes a bit of passing - Oisin Murphy, rider.

See The Fire travelled strongly, but she got there sooner than Oisin wanted to. She just tired late on but she is an exciting filly, and we are looking forward to next year. I think we will look towards the 1,000 Guineas with her - Andrew Balding, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Tiber Tiger British EBF "Newcomers'' Maiden Fillies' Stakes (For horses which have never run) (GBB)
quotes.notes: See The Fire is the best specimen we've had out of Arabian Queen so far and we came here confident as her homework had been exceptional. We'll probably stick to seven furlongs for now, but she has a big future all right - David Bowe, owner's racing manager.

It's been a big team effort with this horse as he's as quirky as they come. Seven Questions spent the night at the racecourse last night as we know when he gets on the horsebox, he gets very stirred up. So, he had an away night about half a mile from his stable. We saddled him about an hour ago and brought him down - he was trying to kick everyone. He's a talented horse on his day and got a brilliant ride. We'll have to re-evaluate where we go now as he was very much at a crossroads. We'll have to see whether he is a Royal Ascot horse - George Scott, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He ran an absolute blinder at Chester the other day when fourth behind Roman Dragon - he showed phenomenal speed from the inside gate, which he needed to do, and tanked along beautifully. I'm going to keep him quite busy - I think he's very well handicapped and if he does win a handicap - which I'm sure he will - he could then go on and win one or two quite cosily. He's frighteningly well handicapped and will be dangerous in any race he shows up in. He runs at Goodwood on Friday. 20-05-26

quotes.notes: Shagraan is improving all the time. He's still growing and filling out and I think he'll be even better next year. We'll put him away now and look to next spring. He loves his racing and hopefully next year he'll be a Group horse. Kieran [Shoemark] gave him a great ride, he's not ridden many for me before but he did exactly as we told him and it was a great job - Mick Appleby, trainer.

Shagraan was drawn on the wrong side and the ground was a bit on the softer side than ideal, but he's done it well. He's still improving and places like Bahrain might suit him, so we'll have a look at where we're going to go - Mick Appleby, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Anderson Roofing Supplies Ltd 20th Anniversary Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.notes: Shagraan has taken a big step forward from his Haydock run and shown a bit of class. We thought he was a horse who could run in a decent grade and he's shown that there. We'll stay at six furlongs for now. Windsor is a nice, sharp track and he was always travelling smoothly and he picked up well. He'll come forward again for that - Clive Cox, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He's a strong and competitive colt by a great sire in Sioux Nation. He made a pleasing second start when an impressive winner at Windsor over 6f, where he travelled strongly throughout. We upped him in class to Listed level last month for the Rose Bowl at Newbury where he stepped up with his performance in finishing a good second. On his homework I think 6f is his strip but he is sharp and ideally he would probably be at his best over 5½f, which leads me to think of the Flying Childers, which we won with Caturra in 2021, who had previously won the Rose Bowl on his way to that Group 2 success. This fellow is definitely going the right way and he runs in the Group 3 Molecomb Stakes at Glorious Goodwood on Wednesday. 02-08-23

quotes.notes: I thought it was a nice performance, Shaihaan travelled and picked up well. He was pretty fit for today but he's a huge horse and this trip was going to suit and he'll improve. He'll head for the Leopardstown Derby Trial, he won't be an Epsom horse but could be one for the Irish Derby - Donnacha O'Brien, trainer, speaking to Racing TV.

I'd love to know where this improvement has come from. Ben [Coen] says the ground is key to Shaool. She had been training really well - all the horses are going well.   I don't think there is anything left for her, she's been busy. I thought today would tell us if she'd come back next year. She's a remarkable filly. She's tough and hardy and works well every day. It was a brilliant performance - Johnny Murtagh, trainer.Shaool was a little bit slow away from the stalls but I thought we went even enough for the ground. She's a filly who you just leave alone for the first half and she starts coming from halfway. Once the gaps opened from three and a half [furlongs] down she was taking them and I hit the line good and strong. Ryan [Moore] said she was green from the two [furlong pole] to the one but said she started to go again in the last furlong. She could be an Albany filly and I imagine she won't mind going up to seven [furlongs] - Aidan O'Brien, trainer, speaking to Racing TV.
Sun Goddess is a lovely filly. We'll try and get one more run into her and, hopefully she turns into an Ascot filly - Aidan O'Brien

quotes.notes: Sunly is a super filly and she's done that on class alone. She's a filly for 2,400 metres [a mile and a half] who doesn't show a whole lot in the mornings but, as you saw there, she was accelerating all the way up the home straight. For now there's no reason to take on the colts and I want to win a fillies' Group 1 with her. I don't know whether we'll stay in France next or go to Britain or Ireland, but her main target would be a race like the Prix Vermeille or the Yorkshire Oaks - Francis Graffard, trainer.

Sunly has been quite a backward filly and she took a long time to come in her coat this spring. What she has done so far has been down to her class and Christophe [Soumillon] said she has really progressed since her last start. She could head to Ascot for the Ribblesdale or wait for the Irish Oaks at the Curragh. It's not impossible she could run in both, but there's the option to wait until the autumn with her. She would be among the favourites for the Ribblesdale and that could be a good option - Francis Graffard, trainer.

Then when he did get a gap another horse squeezed him up. I think he's a little bit unlucky there. I knew he should not have been outsider of the pack as his work had improved since Ascot. He stayed well and the ground is slower, that's the key to him. Every time he's run it's always been pretty quick ground, and Cliff has always come in and said it's on the fast side for him, he's feeling it. He's a lovely honest horse and hopefully we can nick one of these somewhere. The Gimcrack is a possibility if it's nice ground - he's up to that level - Karl Burke, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He's a possible runner in the Windsor Castle after his good second in a Listed race in France. He probably wants a bit more juice in the ground. 12-06-25

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He's always shown a considerable amount of talent but sort of lost his way. He had a wind operation and we gelded him last year. I was thrilled with the way he came back, behaving very well at Southwell and winning in impressive fashion considering he carried a four-year-old's weight. He runs at Pontefract on Wednesday. He looks to have got a little bit quicker and I hope he'll continue to progress along the handicap route. He's a very good mover and, touch wood, very sound. I wouldn't want to run him on rattling fast ground, but equally he doesn't want to run on very soft ground either. We're still learning a little bit with him after only five runs but his behaviour last time was fantastic, which is the important thing with him. 30-04-25

quotes.notes: That was a good performance as she's been off a while and Survie hadn't won for two years. She's effective at this trip, but I think ten furlongs-plus is her trip and I knew she'd finish the race off well - George Boughey, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Sumbe Prix Jean Romanet (Group 1) (3yo+ Fillies & Mares) (Round Course) (Turf)
quotes.notes: The filly has run like a champion. She has an enormous heart and gives everything. Unfortunately, we were done no favours by the draw and she was quite a long way back when the race started in earnest. When you look at the sectionals, Survie has finished fastest of all. I think she stays further and the Royallieu and the Arc are both options we'll discuss with the owners. The real question mark is over the Vermeille, which is only a fortnight away - Nicolas Clement, joint trainer.

We're very happy with Survie's comeback as we knew she would need this race. We thought she would be second to Aventure and she'll come on a lot for this. She picked up very nicely and it's good to see she still has that change of gear. I think she looks better as a four-year-old and the dream is still very much still alive. The programme for her is still wide open and we're still deciding between 2,000 metres and 2,400 metres. Stephane Pasquier said she might be better over 2,000 metres and we'll also hope not to run into Aventure again - Flo Hermans, joint-trainer.

It was a tactical race, but Stephane was in the right place and Survie knows how to quicken. She is in the Arc, she will have a break and could possibly run in the Prix Vermeille first - Nicolas Clement, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: We decided to experiment with her trip a little bit and ran her in the Snowdrop Fillies' Stakes last week over a mile. After getting so far back in the run, she finished really quickly, and I think we'll see a different horse on Guineas weekend, when she'll go for the Dahlia Stakes. She's shown plenty of pace. She was bought to win a Group 1 and our plan is to work through the grades. The New York Stakes at Saratoga in June stands out in the foreign calendar, while there's a brilliant British programme in the second half of the year. 02-04-26

quotes.raceTitle: Longines Sagaro Stakes (Group 3) (A Gold Cup Trial)
quotes.notes: Sweet William is a year older, but he still retains all his enthusiasm. They pulled a long way clear of the third there, but he likes to keep you guessing. He got there, hit the front, and he was happy to stay there rather than go away, but it was a very good performance. We'll see how he comes out of it. The natural thing to do would be to wait for the Gold Cup. There are options beforehand, but we'll discuss it with Mrs Phillipa Cooper and make a plan from there. He's a character and he certainly enjoys himself at home and on the track - Thady Gosden, joint-trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Qipco British Champions Long Distance Cup (Group 1)
quotes.notes: I thought going past the two-furlong pole that I'd got Trawlerman, He looked like he was tying up but I think he went again and a furlong out I tied up a little bit. It was run at a fast pace and I'd say that was a career best from Sweet William. He's quirky but so consistent, and he's my favourite horse of all time. We tried to ease off him after Doncaster but he was swinging Bradley, who rides him every morning, around like a Rag Doll, so we had to kick on with him again, and I'm glad we did. He's a great horse to ride - Rab Havlin, jockey.I was hoping the outsider would spoil it for Trawlerman and soften him up, but he didn't. Rab said he thought he was going to win but Trawlerman found that little bit extra. There was certainly no case of, 'If only'. I can only judge it on how close Sweet William finished to Trawlerman, but the way he picked up I totally agree it was a career best. He picks up and tries now, whereas before he was called bad names for not trying, but you couldn't say that now. Obviously, we'll be careful with his races, but he's run six times this season and he'll be back next year - Philippa Cooper, owner-breeder.

quotes.raceTitle: Betfred Howard Wright Doncaster Cup Stakes (Group 2)
quotes.notes: It's lovely to win this race with Sweet William. It's in memory of Howard Wright who was a great friend of all of us. He was a super fellow, great for racing - we need him back again. I've already been instructed that's it for the season. See you this time next season, same place. Philippa Cooper [owner] wants to go out on a high and build up to the Doncaster Cup next year. They're great these Cup horses, people remember them and enjoy them. Stradivarius, this horse and Trawlerman are exciting for crowds because a lot of our Flat horses disappear too quickly - John Gosden, trainer.
Sweet William will go to Doncaster and that will be it for the year - John Gosden, joint-trainer.

Sweet William will go to York and Doncaster now. A galloping track suits him, maybe a fiddly one like this doesn't. Aidan's runners controlled the early fractions. When they do that, they're very hard to catch - John Gosden, joint-trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Qipco British Champions Long Distance Cup (Group 2) (British Champions Series)
quotes.notes: Sweet William and Trawlerman both ran well. They controlled the pace upfront, both of Aidan's horses. The fractions were pretty steady and then they gradually increased and kicked off the bend. Ours would probably have preferred a stronger, even pace. They've run exceptionally well but Kyprios has a gear more than the rest. I'd have thought we'd come back with both of them next year. They're lovely horses. They both have great enthusiasm for it still and these long-distance horses make it fun - John Gosden, joint-trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Betfred Howard Wright Doncaster Cup Stakes (Group 2) (British Champions Series)
quotes.notes: We've been mucking about with different things and Sweet William seems to be really enjoying it at the minute. We had a visor on and we made the slits slightly bigger so he could see a little bit - just changing things and keeping him interested. He never lets you down but it's nice when he asserts himself like that. He's deserved a big one. He's been in the first three in some top race races - Robert Havlin, rider.

Sweet William has had seven screws in his leg so what a courageous horse. That's why we love him and he's a character. He was box-rested for four months when he was two and he had a hell of a time. I never thought of him being a racehorse, I just wanted him to live. He's the most beautiful horse I've bred and he's named after my son. It's wonderful to be third in a Group 1 and my children don't come racing very often so for them both to run well is wonderful - Philippa Cooper.

It was Philippa's [Cooper, owner] idea to put the visor on Sweet William. We put full-cup blinkers on him last year and he never travelled a yard. He didn't really travel today, to be honest, but the further he went, the better he went. He'll definitely stay two and a half miles and he'll go to Ascot now. He's had a good blow today. He's only run over further than two miles once at Doncaster and it wasn't a test because it turned into a three-furlong sprint. It worked out the way I thought it would in my head. I thought I would let Rossa [Ryan] on Caius Chorister lead me this time because he pounced on me last time. I was able to play with him a little bit up the straight - Rab Havlin, jockey.

Sweet William is becoming more straightforward. He has been a lot of fun to train and it was a long time until he could race for various reasons. He does have a strong view on life and it is not necessarily where you want him to go! He is getting the idea of it well now. The York Ebor meeting might nearly be my favourite meeting of the year, but we have got to get in the race, that's the thing, it will be touch and go. If not, he is a horse who might one day step up the ladder to Cup races - John Gosden, joint-trainer.

We'll take it one race at a time but I think Sweet William would need another penalty to get into the Ebor, and these big handicaps aren't my bag to be honest, but John and Thady Gosden have helped so much with this horse's journey and they will decide - Philippa Cooper, owner/breeder.
Swing Vote ran pretty good, it's a bit sharp for him on this track at a mile. He'll be a nice mile and a quarter horse for over here next year - William Buick, jockey.

I've just spoken to Charlie [Appleby] and we might give him a break now. He was in Dubai over the winter and ultimately he's probably a horse to go back there. We'll see where we go between now and then - Alex Merriam, assistant trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Highclere Castle Gin Carnarvon Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.notes: Dropping back to six furlongs has been the making of Symbol Of Honour. Physically and mentally he's doing well but where we go now I'm not sure. He's not a horse for the Jersey Stakes [over seven furlongs] because I don't think he saw that trip out last time. He's a strong traveller and it's good to get him back on track - Charlie Appleby, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Al Wasl Stakes Sponsored By DP World (Conditions) (Turf)
quotes.notes: Symbol Of Honour had to dig really deep. I think he probably needed the race after a bit of a layoff but I really liked that when he got headed he battled back gamely. The five and six furlong races here, when they meet the intersection and the straight course, the race really starts and we just got caught a little flat-footed there. I think he's more a horse for six-seven furlongs, he's not a horse to drop down in distance - William Buick, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: Bridget 'Confined' Maiden Fillies' Stakes (Newcomers' Race) (GBB Race)
quotes.notes: Synchronicity is obviously expensive, and she's got the pedigree to go with that, but she's been doing all the right things at home and will only improve. Ombudsman is an unbelievable horse, and so far she's following in his footsteps, but I think we'll go up to a mile next. Coming into this season, the plan was here, and if that went well, then the Listed Michael Seely at York could be an option. Whether it comes too soon, I'm not sure, but she's a really exciting filly - Ed Walker, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: She's an exciting filly who's got very big shoes to fill as a sister to Ombudsman. She's extremely attractive and had been working well before her really pleasing debut win at Newbury. She behaved beautifully, Kieran Shoemark gave her an excellent ride and the boys have done a great job on her at home. Her owner Simon Sadler has been very patient with her and we think she's really nice. She has an entry in the Irish 1,000 Guineas but the Michael Seely at York is probably the next conventional step. 22-04-26

quotes.raceTitle: BOYLE Sports Home Of Early Payout Handicap (Div II)
quotes.notes: Syzygy is a nice filly. She had two runs for Danny [McLoughlin, trainer] and he said she'd appreciate the cut in the ground, which probably made the difference today. It slowed things down for her. She was still quite green through the run but picked up and hit the line well so I'd say further will suit her as well. Hopefully she can be progressive on slow ground - Ben Coen, jockey.

That was extremely pleasing. Tabletalk looked the winner the whole way round. He'd been shaping up nicely at home and he seems to be improving.  I was thrilled to see him handle the ground so well, as that was a slight question mark for me, and he stayed on strong over the trip.  He's a very exciting prospect. It's great for the whole team at home who've worked very hard. He ran in the Derby and that was a really tough experience so we gave him a bit of time, he's a big horse and I think he'll make up into a lovely four-year-old.  He has a very patient owner who let me train him where we wanted to go. He ran a very good race at Ascot last time and he's come to himself nicely - Tom Clover, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He ran huge at Newbury on his latest start in the John Porter, just getting touched off by Divina Grace. He's in the Yorkshire Cup but he's also in the Aston Park Stakes back over the course and distance where he ran so well last time. Being a Group 3, that might be a more sensible option than York. The 1m6f at York is quite sharp and he'd see that out fine but he isn't short of speed. He was only just beaten over 1m4f at Newbury on his first start of the year and he's entitled to come on for that run. I hope he can be versatile. 14-05-25

quotes.notes: We came here wanting him to relax and if Talk Of New York got beaten, he got beaten. All we wanted to do was get him to settle and race the right way round. He was back in trip and we applied a hood, which has made a big difference at home. I didn't want to take the hood off but we will next time. We've been lucky in that we've had a few horses gallop here in the last few hours and this fellow would be in the mix of it all. We had the wind taken out of our sails in Dubai, where it all went wrong from the moment he got on the plane. I liked what we've seen today and I wasn't thinking about coming here until William rode him the other day and said we should give him a trial - Charlie Appleby, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Unibet Supports Safer Gambling EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.notes: Talk Of New York was foot perfect in the race. He was a bit babyish, as you'd expect first time out, and a little bit full of himself, but equally he didn't do anything wrong. Once he got relaxed and into a nice rhythm he picked up real good and you'd have to be pretty impressed with what he did there. He's an exciting horse for next year - William Buick, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

quotes.raceTitle: Sky Bet Melrose Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
quotes.notes: I'd say he's a stayer with a future. We'll see what there is for Tarriance in a month's time. Hopefully he's a horse to keep on the team for next year. He might even get a little further, the way he hit the line there. I wouldn't think he'll run in the St Leger - Barry Mahon, Juddmonte racing manager.

quotes.raceTitle: bet365 Very British Raceday Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.notes: It was only Tarriance's second run and he's still a bit inexperienced. He was in the stalls a long time and didn't get the best of starts. But I knew he stays really well and he was the best horse in the race. He's got a great attitude. He's a big, raw horse and he'll probably get further in time - P J McDonald, jockey.

quotes.notes: Tattycoram was always a filly we liked, a proper model and as good a homebred as you'd come across. Very attractive. I'd say last year she was a bit fiery at the gates and we were just trying to stay on the right side of her. She had a good reintroduction at Yarmouth and I thought it was a good effort today. I'd say we'll play our cards on how she is in the coming weeks. I wouldn't rule out the Oaks entry she now has at all, but whatever we do will be with her best interests in mind rather than those of her trainer or owner. I'd love to see her at Epsom but that will depend on how she is over the next four or five weeks. We could have a look at Lingfield perhaps - Ralph Beckett, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: She did well last year when winning a Sandown maiden and getting black type. She's done very well physically from three to four and we expect her to improve. 27-04-26

quotes.notes: Ten Bob Tony has always gone well fresh. He's very tough and gelding him has probably made him a bit more of a man. He's grown up a lot over the winter and he's getting towards being the finished article - Matty Hicks, assistant trrainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: I was a little disappointed with him in the Gladness Stakes but conditions were really testing and it was very hard to make up ground. It was also no coincidence that the winner was the only one who'd had a run this year or that he was ridden more positively than us. He's in great nick and might step up to a mile to see how he gets on. We may look at the bet365 Mile. 22-04-26

quotes.raceTitle: BetBuilder On Football At BetVictor EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.notes: That's Amore is a sister of Richard Hannon's Persica, so she'll get a mile and a quarter, and we'll see how she's working in the spring before maybe starting her in an Oaks trial and go from there. This is generally a good race and normally it throws up a good filly or two. Secret Gesture came out of this race 12 years ago. I'm not saying she's as good as her, but if she's got some of her ability then we'll be all right - Ralph Beckett, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: She made a good start at Southwell last month and could go for the Nottinghamshire Oaks on Sunday. She's been working well and it looks a good fit for her. She kicked a wall and broke her pedal bone after the Cheshire Oaks last year, so it was good to get her going again at Southwell. I think she'll take her racing well. 27-04-26

We still have to make our mind up whether we travel over the winter but he is certainly a horse we'll look forward to next year - Andy Oliver, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He'll probably come back for the Bold Lad Sprint Handicap on Sunday week at the Curragh. He hasn't run since May as he came out of Naas a bit jarred, which was unusual and disappointing. He's had his break since and is fresh and well. He looks to be fully himself. It's his first run back but he normally runs well fresh. We were going to run him this weekend at Navan but we decided we'd go straight for the Curragh. 11-09-24

He'll go to the Lockinge too - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.notes: The Lion In Winter was a bit green, he wasn't sure of himself out in front - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Prix Jean Prat (Group 1) (3yo Colts & Fillies) (Straight Course) (Turf)
quotes.notes: I'm very happy, The Lion In Winter ran a very good race. He has plenty of speed and has the choice of the Sussex or coming back here for the mile race [Jacques le Marois], depending on how he is - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Betfred Derby (In Honour Of His Highness Aga Khan IV) (Group 1) (No Geldings)
quotes.notes: That was disappointing as The Lion In Winter was beaten a long way out - Colin Keane, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: Al Basti Equiworld Dubai Dante Stakes (Group 2)
quotes.notes: Ryan was very happy. He said The Lion In WInter jumped out and he was a bit keen and a bit fresh, but when he did get him back he relaxed very well. He said he had to come out earlier than he wanted as they were coming around him and he probably got a little bit tired because it was his first run, but he was very positive about him. Ryan said the ground probably couldn't be quick enough for him and he rides like a horse with a lot of class and a lot of speed, and we just have to decide now do we go to Epsom or does he go to a French Derby or what does he do? The long and the short of it and what is going to tell us is how he is in a week - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

The Lion In Winter broke smart there and Ryan gave him a very uncomplicated, straightforward ride. They just went an even gallop but he found plenty when Ryan asked him. He looks a very nice colt so I'm delighted for everyone. We always thought he'd get further than seven. We came here with the view he'd go back [to the Curragh] for the Goffs Million and we'd get good experience by coming here. He's not short of pace but you'd imagine he'd get further than a mile and a quarter - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Juddmonte Chaldean Irish EBF (C & G) Maiden
quotes.notes: The Lion In Winter is a lovely horse and had been working lovely. He will have no problem going up in trip but he has plenty of class - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

My gut feeling coming here today was that she probably won't run over a mile again but she saw it out well today and hit the line strong in the Rockfel. Seven furlong options are few and far between and I don't really want to make her a sprinter. She relaxed well today and I think we stay at a mile. She's not won a Stakes race yet. The Coronation Stakes is the obvious race for her, but the question is do we try and get a win into her? She is also entered in the Commonwealth Cup at Royal Ascot - Ed Walker, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Weatherbys Global Stallions App EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.notes: The Prettiest Star was very cool and calm, unlike myself, and pretty professional. She quickly got up to the front-runners and did the job nicely. It's one thing breeding a horse, but another breeding one from a stallion you bred and that's the first one you've run. I'm absolutely delighted. Ed's [Walker, trainer] very considerate of the two-year-olds so we give them plenty of time. This is my first two-year-old runner of the season and she happens to be by Starman. Of late she was looking like she was ready for a race. It's a nice track, a nice opportunity and it's worked out - David Ward, owner-breeder, speaking to Racing TV.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: She's another exciting filly who's done well over the winter and we were very happy with her second away day on the Rowley Mile last week. She had a good blow and that should put her spot on for the 1,000 Guineas. We think she's good enough to go for that and we think she'll stay. She looked very streetwise when second in the Rockfel Stakes and that was her first proper race. Touch wood, her prep has gone well so far. 22-04-26

quotes.notes: The only bit of a setback we had with Thesecretadversary was at Ayr last year. He was a bit unlucky in Canada last time. He's in everything so we'll see where we go. He stays well. He's been working well. He ran a good race at Ascot last year and won well at Tipperary, where he beat the horse who was second in the Middle Park [Brussels], so it was a fair bit of form. He's in every Guineas bar the Italian, and I entered him in a $1 million race in the US the same day as the English Guineas. We'll talk to the owners - Fozzy Stack, trainer.

Thesecretadversary ran a great race. It's annoying we didn't get there, but he ran a great race. He's been very straightforward, he's always looked a bit above average from the minute we started doing a bit with him. I know he's quite colourful, but he's actually a very good model. Seamie was delighted with him, he said he has the pace of a good horse, he feels he will mature in time - Fozzy Stack, trainer.

Thunderbear is a legend. He's been great for us and won a Group 3 at Newbury last year. He's actually developing into a nice sprinter as he gets older. He'd been a bit disappointing this season so it was nice to put him back into calmer waters and get the win. Hopefully we can build from here - Jack Davison, trainer.

I think he's a progressive sprinter and there should be more options on similar ground before the end of the season - Jack Davison, trainer

quotes.notes: Time To Turn didn't run any sort of a race last time and this is much more like him. He's a strong traveller, he goes through the ground well and I thought he put up a good performance. There was never a moment's worry and he's quite a talented horse. He ran in the Lagardere for a good reason and we're back on track. I think you'd be looking at mile options to start with next term and then building him up - William Buick, jockey.

Time To Turn got chinned at Newbury last time on turf, so we dropped him in and rode him to come home the right way and he's done it nicely. Will [Buick] said it slightly happened away from him but we're happy enough. He's pretty straightforward, so Charlie [Appleby] just felt to give him the one run at the field and it has worked out well. We've won this a few times now, but there's no immediate plans for him yet. This was the early target and we'll have a little regroup and see how he slots in with the rest of them, there's quite a few 7f types, so it's just a case of how he fits in. Will was very happy, he said he has a good turn of foot but to stick to 7f. He's really strengthened up for his first couple of runs - Alex Merriam, assistant to Charlie Appleby, trainer.
The ground was too quick for Timeforshowcasing. She's a big filly and very upright. We'll go the German Guineas with her now, which should really suit her - Charlie Johnston, trainer.

Timeforshowcasing is a filly we always loved last year. She won her first two, we probably asked her questions she maybe wasn't quite ready for at the time in Group company but then when she stepped down in class slightly she won well at Goodwood. We made all the ambitious entries for her this year, she's in the Guineas and Irish Guineas, and felt we had to come somewhere to warrant going to one of those. This was the obvious starting point and I'm delighted she's gone and done the job. We'll see what the owners want to do but she wouldn't be out of place turning up in the Guineas. She'd have a bit to find with the principals but she's very straightforward with a great mentality, she was tough there when she needed to be and she stays well - Charlie Johnston, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: Her work in the lead up to the Burradon Stakes had been good and we went there pretty confident, despite the market disagreeing with us. She looked like she was going to get collared 150 yards out, but when the second got to her, she pulled out more and battled on well. That's given us the right to be more audacious in where we go next, and she'll probably go for the 1,000 Guineas. If she finished in the first six we'd be delighted, and I think she's tailor-made for the German Guineas after that. She wouldn't mind some dig in the ground and there's a nice gap between the two races. I think she'd have a good chance in a race like that. 21-04-26

quotes.raceTitle: Qipco British Champions Long Distance Cup (Group 1)
quotes.notes: Trawlerman was at his imperious best in the Gold Cup, but today he might not have been totally. Sweet William ran a blinder, and they're two lovely, staying horses, who are part of the family at home. He came into the straight and probably idled a bit, but on the other hand, the other horse was running him down. The crowd made a hell of a roar because they saw the pink colours and thought he was going to get Trawlerman. It was a great performance from both of them - John Gosden, joint-trainer.Trawlerman is a joy to ride. He's a superstar and I'm delighted for him that he can cap his year off in such a style. He goes out there and wears his heart on his sleeve, and he's a proper horse - William Buick, jockey.
We'll freshen Trawlerman up and he'll run one more time this year at Ascot on Champions day - John Gosden, joint-trainer.

Trawlerman did it in the Henry II and I said to William [Buick] 'try and do the same, set your own pace, pick it up all the way'. He's such a lovely horse. Sweet William didn't quite stay, he's a two and a quarter-mile horse. I said 'look, it's the golden rule, when they come by you they know they've been in a two and a half-mile race' and they never got to him. There's no point going steady like we did in Dubai. I didn't enjoy it [the final furlong] because anything can happen, you never know until they cross the line - John Gosden, joint-trainer.Trawlerman is a great horse. We tried it [same tactics] last year and we were only beaten by the great Kyprios. He's been such a good horse, he's so genuine. John and Thady's [Gosden] horses are in great shape. I was so happy with this fellow when he won at Sandown so he had a beautiful prep into this and he was just so smooth throughout the race; he's really what you want in a two and a half-mile race. I didn't have to touch the brakes once, he was in a nice rhythm and he was relaxed; he went on autopilot, he knows his own speed and he stays well so I was just a passenger. First Gold Cup, it's been a long time coming and it's not an easy race to win - William Buick, jockey.

It was a small field and the plan was just to go to the front with Trawlerman and just let him find a rhythm, which William [Buick] did very well. Last year we gave him a full break from Dubai until Ascot, but this time we thought a prep run would suit him well. He's not having an overly hard blow and he did it well. It's unfortunate news for Ballymore about Kyprios, no one likes to see a horse retired especially at the start of the Flat season, but of course it changes the dynamics of the staying division this year. Trawlerman wears his heart on his sleeve every time and he's part of the furniture now. He's a cracking old boy now and hopefully he can win a big one at some point - Thady Gosden, joint-trainer.

Trawlerman was foot-perfect the whole way and when I turned in I thought I had plenty of horse. He kept finding all the way to the line and even when the winner headed me, he came back. It was a huge run and he stayed the trip. I'm sure that [Goodwood] will be his next target. The winner's been there and done it before so you've got to respect him but Trawlerman's run a mighty race - William Buick, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: Qipco British Champions Long Distance Cup (Group 2) (British Champions Series)
quotes.notes: When he [Kyprios] passed me comfortably, I thought he was going to win by a few lengths but when he couldn't get away from me, I thought that maybe there's a little bit left here. In fairness, Trawlerman was a professional today and a great battler - Frankie Dettori, rider.

quotes.raceTitle: Jockey Club Rose Bowl Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.notes: The Rose Bowl is a nice race to win and we'll have another go at the Ascot race. Trawlerman has to go down early as he takes such a strong grip - John Gosden, joint-trainer.

We did that with Trawlerman's sire Golden Horn in the Arc, we did it with Muntahaa in this race and we've done it again here. Once you get that draw you should just stay out there. It works. It was very much a team decision. As soon as we got that draw we knew what we were going to do. So long as you mind your own business, you're fine. You just don't want the horse to turn right and go into the stables. You had to fancy him to run a big race after his run at Goodwood. I felt very strongly that he was the right horse for the day - John Gosden, joint-trainer.

Trawlerman ran last time at Newmarket and he is over generous. He leans on the rider a bit and doesn't give them much of a chance usually. Obviously he had the hood on today, which helped him a lot, but Benoit gave him a great ride and every time he felt a horse coming to him at the end, he pulled out a little bit more. We were trying to run him in a race that had a big enough field to try and get him settled. He is such a genuine horse, he gives you everything when you ask for it. Hopefully the hood relaxes him a bit and lets him enjoy the quality he has - Thady Gosden, joint-trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: British Stallion Studs EBF "High-Rise" Maiden Stakes (Plus 10 Race)
quotes.notes: Trawlerman has obviously learned from his first two runs and he was pretty push-button round there, it was a nice step forward - James Doyle, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: Virgin Bet A Good Bet Handicap
quotes.notes: I was confident when Tribal Chief broke because he was on terms. He wasn't last time. I took him back to a position I was happy with. He picked up really well and was very willing. He can go quite high on the back of that. He's very straightforward and gave me the feel of a very nice horse who will probably find a few more pounds with a bit more cut in the ground. It's going to be his time of year now and he's going to be very competitive in these bigger handicaps -  Sean Levey, jockey.

Tribal Chief has been quite a green horse, that's why we decided to geld him at the end of the winter to try to get him to progress mentally. Now, he's racing much more professionally, and we can see the improvements. The plan is to give him time to keep on improving. Physically, he's not quite there either, so he'll improve this year and next year as well. In time, he'll stay well. Even though he is from the family of Little Big Bear, there's a fair bit of stamina on the dam's side as well. He'll tackle some longer trips, but we're not sure how much further he'll get - David Menuisier, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He started off the season really well with a second at Newmarket in April behind Bullet Point. I then sent him to France to run in a handicap but he was really disappointing. He came back with a sore foot and an abscess, so he must have been feeling it. Sometimes those take a long time to come through - at the time of the race the horse was fine but afterwards he wasn't himself. At Newcastle last time he had a nightmare as he was trapped with nowhere to go on the rail and in the end he just had a canter. If he handles Goodwood perfectly, and I can't see why he wouldn't, he could be a massive contender in the Golden Mile on Friday. 30-07-25

quotes.notes: True Love is a monster of a filly really. She won the Cheveley Park and then I ran her in the wrong race in America. I ran her in the six [furlong race] when I should have run her in the mile. She's a massive, big, powerful filly. I wouldn't think there's any colts as big and powerful as her, but she has a lot of class, she has a great mind, is a great traveller and she's determined as well. Newmarket is one track in the world where there is nowhere to hide and to get a mile up here you have to really get it, so I'm delighted. Wayne [Lordan] gave her a super ride and only produced her when he had to. Obviously it'll depend on what the lads want to do but I'd imagine you're looking at an Irish Guineas and Coronation - she's a very classy filly. She had a run and that race that she won - it's very unusual - most of our Guineas winners had won that race on the way to here. Any that had a run that was the race they won and they came here. Obviously you couldn't be sure that she was to get a mile. She's a Queen Mary winner which is very unusual for a Queen Mary winner to get a mile. When she was able to win over seven furlongs in Leopardstown on soft ground and got no cover  there was always a chance that she could get it - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.True Love is a big, powerful filly as you could see in the ring. She's quite tall but she has the strength to go with it. I was lucky that she won here last year. She ran over seven furlongs the last day and she got to the line quite well and because she showed so much pace there was always a little question mark over whether she would get the mile. Her homework would suggest that she would, so we came here today confident and hopeful. She jumped and she relaxed beautifully and I went through the race very comfortable and when I asked her to go forward, she got to the line well - Wayne Lordan, jockey.

True Love is a big, pacey filly. Whether she'll get a mile or not, it's hard to know, but Ryan [Moore] said she went through the race very easily, so he was very happy. She's definitely something to look forward to. Depending on how Precise and Diamond Necklace are, she could go to France if she doesn't go to Newmarket. All the possibilities are open - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Tattersalls Sceptre Sessions Cheveley Park Stakes (Group 1) (Fillies)
quotes.notes: True Love is a big powerhouse and is very quick. I wouldn't be sure she'd stay as mile as she's by No Nay Never and he has a big influence for speed, but you never know. She's big, but definitely not short of speed. She could go to America as she travels very strongly. We never know if you get through the winter and into the spring if they're going to stay, and she's got a great constitution and mind - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.We won't know if True Love stay a mile until next year, but she has plenty of speed. She coasted past the furlong and found plenty for pressure. She finished second last time, but she's matured and grown stronger since then. She keeps on changing, so you just won't know what will happen. We see her every day at home, but when I got up on her, I realised then how big she's getting. She's growing into herself and still improving - Wayne Lordan, jockey, speaking to ITV Racing.

Obviously True Love is fast, so we weren't sure she'd get six furlongs. She was a Queen Mary winner, so it was very hard for Ryan not to ride her. Obviously the Phoenix would be there for her as well as the Morny and the Cheveley Park - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

The lads will decide, but you'd imagine True Love will have no problem going six [furlongs], but she is [by] No Nay Never and he's a big influence for speed. Always the Queen Mary winner goes to Deauville [for the Prix Morny] or they go to the Curragh [for the Phoenix Stakes], so they're the two races. There's the fillies' race at the Newmarket [the Duchess of Cambridge Stakes] July festival, but if that'll come too early, I don't know. She had to work hard because she was on her own in that part of the track and the only company she was going to get was in the middle, but Ryan [Moore] slowly let her get out there. She did well really because she was under the pump a long way out but she was strong at the line. She's obviously high class. Walking around the ring she was like a big four-year-old and that's not making light of anything, she's just so scopey and so mature. She's something to look forward to - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.True Love is a tall, scopey girl. She'll be better suited when she goes back to six. She looked a bit different to the rest of them at the start. She's a No Nay Never and they're usually big, strong, powerful fast two-year-olds; she's got all that size but she feels like she'll be better suited when she goes a bit further. She was second first time in a Listed race, beat by a smart filly, and then obviously the colt that beat her won yesterday, so the form was there - Ryan Moore, jockey.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: She was great last year, winning three times including the Queen Mary and the Cheveley Park. She could be trained for a Guineas, even though she's by No Nay Never. We'll give her a chance of getting a mile and there's a chance she could get it. 31-03-26

quotes.notes: I thought it was a lot of weight to give away to Right Here Right Now [stablemate] and he would have been my pick of the four but Two Tribes is the better horse of the four and what a super ride - Phil Cunningham, owner, speaking to Racing Dubai.

Two Tribes didn't have a saddle on his back until Wednesday and he's done very little in the run-up to today. I was happy with what I was seeing and we had to have a go. David [Egan, jockey] seems to have got a great tune out of him last week and this. I thought all three runners had really good chances. I told everyone the same this morning that I couldn't split them, but in the back of your mind you always worry that running a week later is going to be too soon - obviously it wasn't! I was dying to get Run Boy Run back to six furlongs with the visor on and Twilight Calls will win a big one. He was drawn on the wrong side today and has done well to finish where he did. I think we'll have a lot of fun with them - Richard Spencer, trainer.It was a lovely victory last Saturday and we weren't going to run Two Tribes after that, but there was a change of plan on Wednesday. We said we'd keep him to seven furlongs, but it was a big pot and he was going to sneak in at the bottom under a penalty, so we said we'd have a crack at it. It's worked out perfectly. He was a 6,000gns foal and it's great for the stallion to have a winner on a big day at a big festival. The last winner we had here was Rumble Inthejungle in the Molecomb  seven years ago and we've been looking for another ever since - Phil Cunningham, owner.It was easier than last week and one of the smoothest races I've ridden in. It all fell into my lap and there was plenty of speed on my side. The pace Get It and Run Boy Run showed early on meant we had a head start over the far side. It was probably one of the easiest races to predict when Get It is drawn one off the fence because you know he's going to grab the rail and go - David Egan, jockey of Two Tribes.

Two Tribes has been so unlucky. Oisin rode him at Newmarket, when he finished third last time, and his whip got stuck in the reins. We were trying to get him qualified for Ascot, but he needed to win at Doncaster and he finished fourth. We were quietly hopeful today. I thought the seven furlongs here might be too tough for him, but it was a long last furlong - Phil Cunningham, owner.

quotes.raceTitle: Sky Bet Sunday Series Nursery Handicap
quotes.notes: It was a shame that Two Tribes couldn't run in the Windsor Castle Stakes at Royal Ascot as he got withdrawn at the start, but we thought he would have out run his odds that day. Neil Callan rode him the last day and said if he had the blinkers on he thought he could have won that day. We changed the cheekpieces for the blinkers and he has got the job done. We have always liked him, but we will just go through the handicap ranks and see how far he goes - Richard Spencer, trainer.

quotes.notes: As I said here a couple of weeks ago, we were coming here as an Oaks trial and Venetian Lace couldn't have run a much better one than that. She'll definitely stay ten furlongs and she should stay 12 on pedigree. She'll go straight to Epsom now. She got a bit marooned on her own today and maybe if she'd had some company with the first and second she might have got back up for second, but I am still delighted. When she galloped here at the Craven meeting we left feeling we had more of an Oaks filly than a Guineas filly so to finish third in a 1000 Guineas is brilliant - Charlie Johnston, trainer.

Venetian Lace run a great race which was no surprise to us as she's always worked like a nice filly which is why she's run in stakes races all her life. We went to Doncaster last time where she was disappointing but I've lost all confidence in the going description at that track. We came here expecting a top-four finish but given a decent surface she has shown her true colours. We'll work back from the Oaks next year and could bring her back here for the 1,000 Guineas first - Charlie Johnston, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: We campaigned very aggressively after her maiden win and rounded off last season with a great second in the Fillies' Mile. We galloped her at the Craven meeting to try to learn a bit more about how we should be approaching the first half of the season. Through the winter I got the impression that she was going to be more of an Oaks filly than a Guineas filly, but Jason Hart was very happy with her work and I think she'll run in the 1,000 Guineas first. It would be no surprise to see her running in the first four or five and, if she did that, it would be the best possible trial for the Oaks. When you're already rated 108 but believe stepping up in trip is likely to bring more improvement, it's easy to get excited. 21-04-26

quotes.notes: Venetian Sun is a great filly. She gave me my first Group One in France last year and back at six furlongs today, I thought she was the horse to beat. She was a little bit keen, and I was probably a position further back than I wanted to be. When I saw Division come upsides me and then was in front, I always knew I had it in the bag. It almost caught a length out of me, but then my filly came back on the bridle. I just didn't want to be hitting the front too soon - Clifford Lee, rider.

I've only had a brief chat with Cliff [Lee] and he didn't think Venetian Sun stayed. She hit the gates very strong and had no cover ? her draw didn't help. Two out, I thought she was getting on the tail of Venetian Lace, and I thought here we go. But she just petered out in the final furlong and we'll look at going down the Commonwealth Cup route now with her - Karl Burke, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Sumbe Prix Morny (Group 1) (2yo Colts & Fillies) (Straight Course) (Turf)
quotes.notes: Venetian Sun is unbelievable, she does everything so relaxed. I've been saying for a little while that she's a special filly and she's proved it there. Early on in the year she stood out in the string and I said to her owners a month ago, she doesn't quite stand out as much and the others have caught her up a little bit, but she's still got so much ability. She'll be better with easier ground. I was very worried when I walked the ground earlier, it's as quick as I've known it here and I've been coming for a number of years now. That dampened my confidence. She'll be better over an extra furlong as well, I'm convinced of that, so we'll go for the Moyglare next and see where we go from there. It will tell us if she's a Classic filly but she's got to prove it. She's got a temperament to die for - Karl Burke, trainer, speaking on Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.raceTitle: Duchess Of Cambridge Stakes (Sponsored By bet365) (Group 2) (Fillies)
quotes.notes: When Venetian Sun cruised to the front, she went a couple of lengths clear and thought it was all over. Ed's [Walker] horse quickened up nicely and Cliff [Lee] just said Venetian Sun was just dossing a bit in front. She is a filly a bit like that as she's so laidback and I also think the ground was on the quick side for her today. She is a very high-class filly. I think the Lowther would be out for her now as she has won a Group Two. She is in the Prix Morny and we'll have a look at that but we are very keen to step up to seven furlongs in the Moyglare. Her pedigree says she is more a miler at least and a three-year-old. She's a very mature filly with a great engine. I think she can be better on better ground and over a trip. She relaxes so well in behind. I think racing against the very best horses will bring out the best in her - Karl Burke, trainer.

I think Venetian Sun is a a very special filly. The work she has done at home, I haven't had a 2yo filly do work like it; just the last six weeks. She's kicking older group horses out the way at home. I worked a good, old work horse with her about a month ago or just after her debut and I had to work her with another good one that I knew was reliable and she did the same to him and I'm talking 110 rated horses. I think she's very special - Karl Burke, trainer. Karl did say she was the 2yo filly he's had, so we had a lot of confidence in her. So we were confident and happy to back him, and he did a great job with her. I don't think everything went for her - tough draw and she didn't have much cover, so yeah - Ian McAleavy, joint-owner.

quotes.raceTitle: British Stallion Studs EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.notes: Cliff [Lee, jockey] gave Venetian Sun a lovely ride and he said he ended up hitting the front too soon and she was just dossing about a bit in front. It's just greenness and she'll learn loads from that. It was a very good race for the grade and I would say she's very, very useful. If she goes to Royal Ascot it will be the Albany I would think, she's a real six-furlong filly - Karl Burke, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: The top two-year-old filly in Britain last year. I think she was every bit as good as Aidan's [O'Brien] fillies who came on strong late on, whereas we were on the go quite early, and she beat the colts in the Morny. On her last start in the Moyglare, she was beaten two out and it wasn't her true running. She's wintered really well and the plan is to go straight to the Guineas. The key question is whether she'll stay a mile, but if ever a filly was going to, it would be her - I think she's got an 80-90 per cent chance. If that doesn't come to fruition, we can revert back to sprinting. 31-03-26
